observations.title: Fixed RxDB 'Cannot redefine property: deleted$' crash — renamed deleted→is_deleted
observations.content:
**What**: Renamed field `deleted` to `is_deleted` in RxDB schemas, hooks, push/pull handlers, and Supabase columns. `deleted` is a reserved RxDB v17 internal property (docs have `deleted$` getter). Our schema defining `deleted` caused `TypeError: Cannot redefine property: deleted$` crash on subscribe.

**Why**: Playwright captured the error. RxDB v17's replication-protocol module calls `Object.defineProperty` on document prototype for `deleted$`, which fails if schema has a `deleted` field.

**Where**: `src/lib/rxdb.js` (schemas, handlers, hooks), `src/hooks/useWorkOrders.js`, Supabase (3 ALTER TABLE statements). Also applied null-safety, deduplication, and try-catch fixes.

**Learned**: `deleted` is a RESERVED field name in RxDB. Other fixes applied: null-guard in createPullHandler (Supabase can return null data), deduplication of startAllReplications (StrictMode double-mount), COLLECTION_CONFIG for forceResync, try-catch in all subscribe callbacks.

MUI v9 uses `slotProps.input` not `InputProps`. `equipment_id` is primaryKey in equipment_ids schema, and `.findOne()` on RxDB collection is the correct async validation method.

observations.title: Session summary: cmms-ibero
observations.content:
## Goal
Implementar módulo completo offline-first de gestión de activos para CMMS Ibero: creación con validación local RxDB, panel de detalles con JSONB, unificación del árbol a RxDB, y UI con Dialog modal. Dos deploys a producción.

## Instructions
- NO exponer contraseñas en conversación
- Usar Playwright como herramienta principal de verificación (Sentry MCP no operativo)
- No usar --no-verify en git a menos que el usuario lo autorice explícitamente
- GGA pre-commit hook tiene incompatibilidad con opencode en subshell de Windows (límite de argumentos + timeout). Se aplicó parche en providers.sh (stdin pipe) pero sigue sin funcionar en git hooks de Windows.

## Discoveries
- `deleted` es campo RESERVADO en RxDB v17. RxDB crea `deleted$` interno y colisiona con schema. Fix: renombrar a `is_deleted`.
- `TreeView` no existe en @mui/x-tree-view v9. Reemplazo: `SimpleTreeView` con `onItemClick` (no `onNodeSelect`).
- `createPullHandler` intenta ordenar por `id` que no existe en vistas de Supabase. Se creó `createPullHandlerView` sin orden secundario.
- MUI v9 usa `slotProps.input` en vez de `InputProps`. `InputLabelProps` → `slotProps.inputLabel`.
- GGA en Windows: el prompt con 8 archivos excede límite de argumentos de shell (32K). Parche en providers.sh usa stdin pipe como execute_claude.
- Snackbar dentro de Dialog se destruye al cerrar el Dialog. Se usó setTimeout para delay de auto-cierre.
- MUI Select en v9 se abre con `.MuiSelect-select` click, no con `role="combobox"`.

## Accomplished
- ✅ Fix RxDB: `deleted` → `is_deleted` en schemas, hooks, handlers, y 3 ALTER TABLE en Supabase
- ✅ Fix RxDB: null-safety en createPullHandler, deduplicación StrictMode startAllReplications, COLLECTION_CONFIG para forceResync, try-catch en subscribe callbacks
- ✅ Crear vista `equipment_ids` en Supabase + schema RxDB + replicación pull-only
- ✅ Crear `AddAssetForm.jsx`: MUI con validación offline equipment_id contra RxDB local, campos dinámicos por asset_type_id (M-MOT, M-BOM, M-TAN, M-CAL → JSONB technical_specs), inserción con asset_hierarchy
- ✅ Crear `AssetDetailsPanel.jsx`: Drawer 420px derecha, header con Tag/chips, tabla datos base, sección JSONB con humanizeKey
- ✅ Unificar App.jsx a AssetTree RxDB (reemplazar AssetTree Supabase). Marcar src/AssetTree.jsx como DEPRECATED.
- ✅ Conectar tree con panel: onClick directo en labels → abre Drawer con datos
- ✅ Refactor UI: AddAssetForm dentro de Dialog modal con auto-cierre, botón "+ Nuevo Activo" arriba del árbol
- ✅ 9 tests Playwright cubriendo: render, validación offline, submit con auto-cierre, campos dinámicos, panel click, cero errores consola
- ✅ 2 deploys Vercel production: cmms-ibero.vercel.app
- ✅ 2 commits en GitHub: feat + refactor(ui)

## Next Steps
- Configurar Sentry para monitoreo de errores en producción
- Implementar edición de activos desde el panel de detalles
- Considerar actualizar Engram CLI de 1.14.13 a 1.15.4
- Rotar tokens expuestos (GitHub PAT, Sentry token, Supabase password)

## Relevant Files
- src/lib/rxdb.js — Core RxDB: schemas, replication, hooks (useRxDB, useAssets, useWorkOrders)
- src/components/AddAssetForm.jsx — Formulario modal de creación con validación offline
- src/components/AssetDetailsPanel.jsx — Drawer de detalles con render JSONB
- src/components/AssetTree.jsx — Árbol RxDB con SimpleTreeView v9 y onClick
- src/App.jsx — Unificación: RxDB tree + Dialog form + Drawer panel
- src/hooks/useWorkOrders.js — Hook de work orders con RxDB
- tests/home.spec.js — 9 tests Playwright E2E
- scripts/migrate-deleted-column.mjs — Migración Supabase deleted→is_deleted
- scripts/create-equipment-ids-view.mjs — Vista equipment_ids en Supabase
- C:\Users\diego\bin\lib\gga\providers.sh — Parche stdin pipe para opencode en GGA

observations.title: sdd/preventive-condition-core-phase-1/proposal
observations.content:
# Proposal: Preventive & Condition-Based Maintenance — Core Schema Phase 1

## Intent

SQL schema foundation for PM/CBM module. Enables planners to define PM job plans, schedule them against assets (time/meter), and capture condition monitoring data — database layer only.

## Scope

### In Scope

- Migration: `job_plans`, `job_plan_tasks`, `job_plan_materials`
- Migration: `pm_schedules` with time/meter frequency, floating window, suppression chain
- Migration: `meters`, `measure_points`, `meter_readings`
- RLS policies on all 7 tables, role-gated
- CHECK constraints for non-negative freqs, valid values

### Out of Scope

- Triggers, functions, edge functions (Phase 2)
- RxDB schemas, UI, AI signal processing

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

- `pm-job-plan-schema`: job_plans, job_plan_tasks, job_plan_materials
- `pm-schedule-schema`: pm_schedules (time/meter/float/suppression)
- `condition-monitoring-schema`: meters, measure_points, meter_readings

### Modified Capabilities

None — additive schema, no existing spec behavior changes.

## Approach

Single idempotent migration (`supabase/migrations/`). Three groups:

| Group | Tables | Key FK Targets |
|-------|--------|----------------|
| PM Templates | job_plans → job_plan_tasks → job_plan_materials | `spare_parts(part_num)` |
| Schedules | pm_schedules | `assets(id)`, `job_plans(id)`, self-FK suppression |
| Monitoring | meters → measure_points → meter_readings | `assets(id)` |

- `pm_schedules.frequency` as JSONB supporting `{type:"days", value:N}`, `{type:"meter", meter_id:UUID, value:N}`, or `{type:"both"}`
- `suppressed_by` nullable self-FK, deferrable
- RLS: ADMIN/PLANNER full r/w; TECHNICIAN read + insert readings only

## Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|------|------------|------------|
| FK type mismatch with assets(id) TEXT | Low | Use `TEXT REFERENCES assets(id)` — confirmed convention |
| Self-FK suppression update ordering | Low | Make nullable, deferrable |

## Rollback Plan

`DROP TABLE ... CASCADE` all 7 tables. No data loss — tables are new.

## Dependencies

- `assets` table (FK target)
- `spare_parts` table (FK for job_plan_materials)
- `get_user_role()` helper for RLS

## Success Criteria

- [ ] All 7 tables created with correct FK chains
- [ ] CHECK constraints reject negative frequencies/values
- [ ] RLS active on all tables — ADMIN/PLANNER full, TECHNICIAN restricted
- [ ] pm_schedules supports time, meter, and hybrid freq via JSONB
- [ ] Suppression chain enforced via self-FK
- [ ] Migration idempotent — safe to run multiple times

observations.title: sdd/preventive-condition-core-phase-1/spec
observations.content:
# Preventive & Condition-Based Maintenance — Core Schema Specification

## Purpose

Database foundation for PM/CBM module. Defines job plan templates, scheduling rules (time/meter-driven), and asset condition monitoring via meters with threshold-based alerting. Schema-only — no triggers, functions, or application logic.

## Requirements

### Requirement: job_plans Table

The system MUST create a `job_plans` table:

| Column | Type | Constraints |
|--------|------|-------------|
| id | UUID | PK, DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() |
| code | TEXT | UNIQUE NOT NULL |
| description | TEXT | nullable |
| intervention_type | TEXT | NOT NULL, CHECK (IN: 'INSPECTION','LUBRICATION','MINOR_SERVICE','OVERHAUL') |
| estimated_hours | NUMERIC | DEFAULT 0 |
| created_at | TIMESTAMPTZ | DEFAULT NOW() |

#### Scenario: Create a job plan

- GIVEN a valid intervention_type and unique code
- WHEN a planner inserts a job plan
- THEN the row is created with generated UUID and default timestamps

#### Scenario: Duplicate code rejected

- GIVEN a job plan with code 'PM-001' exists
- WHEN inserting another with the same code
- THEN the INSERT MUST fail with unique constraint violation

### Requirement: job_plan_tasks Table

The system MUST create a `job_plan_tasks` table:

| Column | Type | Constraints |
|--------|------|-------------|
| id | UUID | PK, DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() |
| job_plan_id | UUID | NOT NULL, FK → job_plans(id) ON DELETE CASCADE |
| step_sequence | INT | NOT NULL |
| task_description | TEXT | NOT NULL |
| | | UNIQUE(job_plan_id, step_sequence) |

#### Scenario: Add sequenced tasks to a job plan

- GIVEN a job plan exists
- WHEN tasks with sequential step numbers are inserted
- THEN all tasks are persisted in order

#### Scenario: Cascade delete

- GIVEN a job plan with associated tasks
- WHEN the job plan is deleted
- THEN all its tasks are deleted

#### Scenario: Duplicate step sequence

- GIVEN step_sequence 10 is assigned for a job plan
- WHEN inserting another step_sequence 10 for the same job plan
- THEN the INSERT MUST fail with unique constraint violation

### Requirement: job_plan_materials Table

The system MUST create a `job_plan_materials` table:

| Column | Type | Constraints |
|--------|------|-------------|
| id | UUID | PK, DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() |
| job_plan_id | UUID | NOT NULL, FK → job_plans(id) ON DELETE CASCADE |
| part_num | TEXT | nullable, references spare_parts optionally |
| planned_qty | NUMERIC | NOT NULL, CHECK (> 0) |

#### Scenario: Add materials to a job plan

- GIVEN a job plan exists
- WHEN material rows with planned_qty > 0 are inserted
- THEN materials are linked to the job plan

#### Scenario: Zero quantity rejected

- GIVEN a job plan exists
- WHEN inserting a material with planned_qty = 0
- THEN the INSERT MUST fail with CHECK constraint violation

### Requirement: pm_schedules Table

The system MUST create a `pm_schedules` table:

| Column | Type | Constraints |
|--------|------|-------------|
| id | UUID | PK, DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() |
| asset_id | TEXT | NOT NULL, FK → assets(id) |
| job_plan_id | UUID | NOT NULL, FK → job_plans(id) |
| time_frequency_days | INT | nullable |
| meter_frequency_value | NUMERIC | nullable |
| is_floating | BOOLEAN | DEFAULT false |
| parent_schedule_id | UUID | nullable, FK → pm_schedules(id) |
| suppression_multiplier | INT | nullable |
| last_completion_date | TIMESTAMPTZ | nullable |
| next_target_date | TIMESTAMPTZ | nullable |
| created_at | TIMESTAMPTZ | DEFAULT NOW() |

#### Scenario: Time-based PM schedule

- GIVEN an asset and a job plan exist
- WHEN a schedule with time_frequency_days = 30 is created
- THEN next_target_date SHALL be calculated as last_completion_date + 30 days

#### Scenario: Suppression chain

- GIVEN a parent schedule exists
- WHEN a child schedule links via parent_schedule_id with suppression_multiplier = 2
- THEN the child's next_target_date is suppressed until the parent is overdue by 2 cycles

#### Scenario: Meter-driven schedule

- GIVEN time_frequency_days is NULL and meter_frequency_value = 1000
- WHEN the schedule is evaluated
- THEN it triggers based on accumulated meter readings, not calendar days

### Requirement: meters Table

The system MUST create a `meters` table:

| Column | Type | Constraints |
|--------|------|-------------|
| id | UUID | PK, DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() |
| asset_id | TEXT | NOT NULL, FK → assets(id) |
| code | TEXT | NOT NULL |
| meter_type | TEXT | NOT NULL, CHECK (IN: 'CONTINUOUS','GAUGE','CHARACTERISTIC') |
| uom | TEXT | NOT NULL |

#### Scenario: Register a meter on an asset

- GIVEN an asset exists
- WHEN a meter with valid meter_type and uom is inserted
- THEN the meter is linked to the asset for condition tracking

#### Scenario: Invalid meter_type rejected

- GIVEN an asset exists
- WHEN inserting a meter with meter_type = 'VOLTAGE'
- THEN the INSERT MUST fail with CHECK constraint violation

### Requirement: measure_points Table

The system MUST create a `measure_points` table:

| Column | Type | Constraints |
|--------|------|-------------|
| id | UUID | PK, DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() |
| meter_id | UUID | NOT NULL, FK → meters(id) ON DELETE CASCADE |
| upper_limit_warning | NUMERIC | nullable |
| upper_limit_critical | NUMERIC | nullable |
| lower_limit_warning | NUMERIC | nullable |
| lower_limit_critical | NUMERIC | nullable |

#### Scenario: Define thresholds for a meter

- GIVEN a meter exists
- WHEN measure_points with warning and critical limits are inserted
- THEN thresholds are set for condition-based alerting

#### Scenario: Thresholds cascade on meter removal

- GIVEN measure_points exist for a meter
- WHEN the meter is deleted
- THEN all associated measure_points are deleted

### Requirement: meter_readings Table

The system MUST create a `meter_readings` table:

| Column | Type | Constraints |
|--------|------|-------------|
| id | UUID | PK, DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() |
| meter_id | UUID | NOT NULL, FK → meters(id) ON DELETE CASCADE |
| reading_value | NUMERIC | NOT NULL |
| reading_date | TIMESTAMPTZ | DEFAULT NOW() |
| is_alert_triggered | BOOLEAN | DEFAULT false |

#### Scenario: Record a meter reading

- GIVEN a meter exists
- WHEN a numeric reading_value is inserted
- THEN the reading is stored with auto-generated timestamp

#### Scenario: Historical readings retrieval

- GIVEN multiple readings exist for a meter across different dates
- WHEN querying ordered by reading_date DESC
- THEN the full reading history is returned with the most recent first

### Requirement: RLS Access Control

The system MUST enable RLS on all 7 tables. ADMIN and PLANNER SHALL have full read/write on all tables. TECHNICIAN SHALL have SELECT on all tables and INSERT only on `meter_readings`.

#### Scenario: ADMIN full access

- GIVEN an authenticated user with role ADMIN
- WHEN performing any DML on any table
- THEN the operation succeeds

#### Scenario: TECHNICIAN inserts reading

- GIVEN an authenticated user with role TECHNICIAN
- WHEN inserting into meter_readings
- THEN the operation succeeds

#### Scenario: TECHNICIAN denied on job_plans INSERT

- GIVEN an authenticated user with role TECHNICIAN
- WHEN attempting to INSERT into job_plans
- THEN the RLS policy rejects the operation

## Non-Functional Requirements

- **Idempotency**: All CREATE TABLE statements MUST use IF NOT EXISTS for safe re-runs
- **FK integrity**: All foreign keys MUST be strict (no ON DELETE SET NULL) except as noted
- **Constraint enforcement**: CHECK constraints MUST reject invalid values at database level
- **No triggers/functions**: Business logic is deferred to Phase 2

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `job_plans`, `job_plan_tasks`, `job_plan_materials` created with FK chain to each other and `spare_parts`
- [ ] `pm_schedules` created with FK to `assets(id)`, `job_plans(id)`, and nullable self-FK for suppression
- [ ] `meters`, `measure_points`, `meter_readings` created with FK chain to `assets(id)`
- [ ] CHECK constraints reject negative planned_qty, invalid intervention_type, and invalid meter_type
- [ ] UNIQUE(job_plan_id, step_sequence) enforced on job_plan_tasks
- [ ] RLS enabled on all 7 tables — ADMIN/PLANNER full r/w, TECHNICIAN restricted
- [ ] Migration idempotent — safe to run repeatedly

observations.title: Architectural rules: PM/RCM engine design constraints
observations.content:
**What**: Three permanent architectural rules for the PM/RCM engine, persisted for all future decisions

**Why**: User explicitly requested these be saved to Engram as non-negotiable design constraints

**Where**: Applied in supabase/migrations/20260522000001_preventive_condition_core.sql and ADR-03 (docs/architecture/03-pm-rcm-engine.md)

**Learned**:

**RULE 1 — Math lives in Postgres**: The predictive engine (RCM) uses pure Postgres (PL/pgSQL and pg_cron) for all mathematical and date calculations. NEVER in the frontend. This protects AI algorithms from timezone mismatches and ensures consistency regardless of client state.

**RULE 2 — Separate condition limits from IoT data**: We ALWAYS separate condition thresholds (measure_points) from high-volume IoT data (meter_readings). This prevents lock contention during data bursts and keeps the master structure lightweight. SAP/Maximo inspired.

**RULE 3 — Strict RBAC**: Master tables (job_plans, job_plan_tasks, job_plan_materials, pm_schedules, meters, measure_points) can only be modified by PLANNER and ADMIN roles. TECHNICIAN role only inserts transactional data (meter_readings, work_orders). This is non-negotiable — no open policies on master data ever.

observations.title: sdd/seed-epicor-script/proposal
observations.content:
# Proposal: Seed Epicor Script

## Intent

Create a self-contained Node.js script that ingests a raw Epicor data dump (~300 assets, ~150 hierarchy relations) into the CMMS database. The file has non-standard formatting (interleaved CSV blocks, escaped underscores, truncated JSON) that requires parsing and healing before insertion. This avoids manual data entry and provides a repeatable migration path for future Epicor imports.

## Scope

### In Scope
- Single script `scripts/seed_epicor.js` with zero external dependencies
- CSV parser that respects quoted fields (commas in `technical_specs`)
- Data healing: unescape `\_` → `_` in JSON, truncated JSON → `{}` fallback
- Dynamic `asset_types` upsert: extract codes → upsert → map IDs
- Bulk insert of ~300 `assets` with correct FK references to `asset_types`
- Build `equipment_id → id` mapping, insert ~150 `asset_hierarchy` rows
- `--dry-run` flag: validate parsing & counts without DB writes
- Config via env vars (`SUPABASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`)

### Out of Scope
- Scheduling or automation (cron, webhook triggers)
- Dedicated error recovery (re-run in dry-run first)
- Incremental sync with Epicor (one-shot seed only)
- UI or admin panel for re-seeding

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities
- `data-seeding`: Script-based bulk ingestion of master data (assets, types, hierarchy) from CSV sources into the CMMS database.

### Modified Capabilities
- None

## Approach

Pipeline executed in a single script run:

1. **Read & Parse** — read file, split by blank lines into blocks, identify block type by header, parse CSV with quoted-field support
2. **Heal** — regex-replace `\_` with `_` in raw values; for `technical_specs`, detect truncated JSON via incomplete parse → substitute `{}`
3. **Dry-run** — if `--dry-run`, log parsed block counts, row counts, distinct asset_type codes, and first/last row samples; exit
4. **Upsert asset_types** — collect unique codes from data, upsert each, build `code → id` map via INSERT ... ON CONFLICT ... RETURNING
5. **Insert assets** — map each row: heal fields, resolve `asset_type_id` FK, POST to Supabase REST API or batch insert
6. **Insert hierarchy** — wait for all assets inserted, build `equipment_id → id` map, POST hierarchy rows

## Affected Areas

| Area | Impact | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `scripts/seed_epicor.js` | New | Standalone seed script, zero deps, run with `node scripts/seed_epicor.js --dry-run` |

## Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|------|------------|------------|
| Truncated or malformed JSON beyond `{}` fallback | Low | Dry-run surfaces parse issues before writes; log warnings per row |
| FK mismatch on `asset_type_id` | Low | Upsert ensures types exist; error on missing code fails fast |
| Duplicate `equipment_id` on re-run | Medium | Use upsert on `equipment_id` (ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE) or truncate first |
| Network failure mid-insert | Medium | Re-run in dry-run first; script is idempotent with upserts |

## Rollback Plan

- **Before run**: take a pg_dump of `assets`, `asset_types`, `asset_hierarchy`
- **If partial failure**: re-run script — upserts make it idempotent
- **If full revert needed**: `TRUNCATE asset_hierarchy, assets, asset_types CASCADE` then restore from dump

## Dependencies

- Node.js 18+ (native `fetch`)
- `SUPABASE_URL` and `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` env vars
- Raw data file at repo root (already exists)

## Success Criteria

- [ ] `node scripts/seed_epicor.js --dry-run` prints valid counts and samples without errors
- [ ] `node scripts/seed_epicor.js` inserts all assets and hierarchy correctly (verified by row count queries)
- [ ] FK constraints satisfied (no orphaned asset rows, no orphaned hierarchy rows)
- [ ] `technical_specs` JSON is valid for every row (no parse errors)
- [ ] Running the script a second time produces identical state (upsert idempotency)

observations.title: sdd/seed-epicor-script/spec
observations.content:
# Data-Seeding Specification

## Purpose

One-shot bulk ingestion of master data (assets, types, hierarchy) from raw Epicor CSV dumps into the CMMS database. The script MUST parse non-standard formatting, heal data artifacts, validate before writing, and produce a consistent database state idempotently.

## Requirements

### Requirement: CSV Parsing

The script MUST parse interleaved CSV blocks from a single file. Each block MUST be identified by a header line. Fields enclosed in double quotes MUST be treated as single values (commas inside quotes are NOT field separators). Blank lines MUST delimit blocks.

#### Scenario: Happy path block parsing

- GIVEN a file with an ASSET block and a HIERARCHY block separated by a blank line
- WHEN the script reads the file
- THEN each block is parsed into the correct number of rows AND fields respect quoted-value boundaries

#### Scenario: Commas inside quoted technical_specs

- GIVEN a CSV row where `technical_specs` contains `"{""voltage"":""230V,50Hz""}"`
- WHEN the CSV parser processes the row
- THEN the quoted field is consumed as a single value, NOT split at the comma

### Requirement: Data Healing

The script MUST unescape `\_` sequences → `_` in all string values. For the `technical_specs` column, if the JSON is truncated (parse fails), the script MUST substitute the value with `{}`.

#### Scenario: Unescape underscored text

- GIVEN a `description` field containing `motor\_type\_A`
- WHEN healed
- THEN the stored value is `motor_type_A`

#### Scenario: Truncated JSON fallback

- GIVEN a `technical_specs` cell containing `{"voltage":"230V","power"` (truncated)
- WHEN healed
- THEN the stored value is `{}`

### Requirement: Dry-Run Mode

The script MUST support a `--dry-run` flag. When set, the script MUST parse all blocks, heal all data, validate row counts and distinct asset_type codes, and report findings — but MUST NOT execute any INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE against the database.

#### Scenario: Dry-run validates before write

- GIVEN `--dry-run` is passed
- WHEN the script runs
- THEN output includes parsed block types, row counts per block, distinct asset_type codes, and samples of first/last rows — AND zero rows are written to the database

### Requirement: Asset Types Upsert

The script MUST collect unique asset_type codes from the parsed data. For each code, it MUST perform an upsert (INSERT ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING). After upsert, it MUST build a `code → id` mapping for FK resolution.

#### Scenario: Duplicate codes are deduplicated

- GIVEN the data contains 10 rows, all with `asset_type_code = "PUMP"`
- WHEN upserting asset_types
- THEN exactly one row exists in `asset_types` for code `"PUMP"` AND the map returns the same ID for all 10 rows

### Requirement: Assets Insert

The script MUST insert every parsed asset row with a resolved `asset_type_id` FK. Each asset MUST be identified by `equipment_id` for upsert purposes (ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE).

#### Scenario: Full asset ingest

- GIVEN ~300 parsed rows after healing
- WHEN the script inserts assets
- THEN all rows are inserted AND every row has a valid non-null `asset_type_id` AND no orphan rows exist (FK constraint satisfied)

#### Scenario: Duplicate equipment_id on re-run

- GIVEN the script has already been run once
- WHEN it runs again with the same data
- THEN no duplicate key error occurs AND the final row count matches the original run (upsert idempotency)

### Requirement: Hierarchy Insert

After all assets are inserted, the script MUST build a `equipment_id → asset_id` map and insert `asset_hierarchy` rows. A row MUST link a parent asset to a child asset using their `equipment_id` values from the source data.

#### Scenario: Hierarchy correctly linked

- GIVEN the data defines parent `PLANT-01` and child `PUMP-001`
- WHEN hierarchy rows are inserted
- THEN the `asset_hierarchy` table contains a row where `parent_id` is the asset ID for `PLANT-01` AND `child_id` is the asset ID for `PUMP-001`

#### Scenario: Missing hierarchy reference

- GIVEN a hierarchy row references `equipment_id` "MISSING-ASSET" that does not exist in the assets data
- WHEN hierarchy insert runs
- THEN the script MUST log a warning and skip that row (not fail the entire batch)

### Requirement: Error Handling

The script MUST fail fast on unrecoverable errors: unreadable file, missing env vars, DB connection failure. On recoverable errors (truncated JSON, missing hierarchy refs), the script MUST log a warning and continue.

#### Scenario: Missing env var fails fast

- GIVEN `SUPABASE_URL` is not set
- WHEN the script attempts to run (without `--dry-run`)
- THEN the script exits immediately with a non-zero code and a descriptive error message

observations.title: sdd/seed-epicor-script/design
observations.content:
# Design: Seed Epicor Script

## Technical Approach

A single self-contained Node.js script (`scripts/seed_epicor.js`) that reads the interleaved CSV data file, heals formatting issues, and inserts data into Supabase via REST API. Runs with `node scripts/seed_epicor.js [--dry-run]` — zero npm dependencies, uses built-in `fetch` + `fs`.

Pipeline: parse .env → read file → split CSV blocks by blank lines → parse each block → heal data → dry-run validation OR upsert asset_types → insert assets → insert hierarchy.

## Architecture Decisions

### Decision: Build with Node.js 18+ built-in fetch, not Supabase JS client

| Option | Tradeoff | Decision |
|--------|----------|----------|
| `@supabase/supabase-js` client | Pulls dep + ESM troubles in standalone script | ❌ Rejected |
| Built-in `fetch` + REST API | Zero deps, same auth (anon key in header), full control | ✅ Chosen |

Rationale: The script runs outside Vite's module resolution. Using raw `fetch` with `POST /rest/v1/{table}?onConflict=code&returnRepresentation=minimal` avoids pulling the entire npm client for a one-shot script.

### Decision: Manual CSV parser, not a library

Rationale: Only ~300 rows. One edge case (quoted fields with internal commas). A 30-line state-machine parser handles it. No `csv-parse` dep needed.

### Decision: Manual .env parser

Rationale: Two flat `KEY=VALUE` lines, no quotes, no comments. `split("=")` with `trim()` is sufficient. No `dotenv` dep.

### Decision: Block-split by blank lines

Rationale: The data file interleaves asset blocks and hierarchy blocks separated by blank lines. Splitting on `\n\n` (one or more blank lines) yields blocks, each starting with a header line that identifies the block type.

### Decision: Upsert via `onConflict` + `Prefer: return=representation`

Rationale: On re-run, `equipment_id` UNIQUE and `asset_types.code` UNIQUE require upsert semantics. The script POSTs with `onConflict` query param and `Prefer: resolution=merge-duplicates, return=representation` headers so we get back the IDs.

### Decision: Service role key vs anon key

Rationale: The script uses `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` from `.env` (not a service role key). RLS is currently disabled on all tables, so the anon key has full access. The `.env` file already contains this key. Using the same key as the frontend avoids requiring additional secrets.

## Data Flow

```
 ┌──────────┐   parseEnv()    ┌──────────────────┐
 │  .env    │ ─────────────→  │ SUPABASE_URL      │
 └──────────┘                 │ SUPABASE_ANON_KEY │
                              └──────────────────┘

 ┌──────────┐   readFile()   ┌───────────────────┐
 │ data.md  │ ────────────→  │ raw string         │
 └──────────┘                └───────────────────┘
                                     │
                            splitBlocks() — split on \n\n
                                     │
                            ┌────────┴────────┐
                            │  asset blocks    │
                            │  hierarchy blks  │
                            └────────┬────────┘
                                     │
                            parseCsvRow() — quoted-field-aware
                                     │
                            healData() — \_ → _, JSON repair
                                     │
                            ┌────────┴────────┐
                            │  --dry-run?      │
                            └────────┬────────┘
                            yes      │      no
                            ↓        │        ↓
                     log & exit      │   upsertAssetTypes()
                                     │   → code→id Map
                                     │
                                     ↓
                               insertAssets()
                               → equipment_id→id Map
                                     │
                                     ↓
                              insertHierarchy()
                              → parent_id/child_id
                                resolved via Map
```

## File Changes

| File | Action | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `scripts/seed_epicor.js` | Create | ~200 LOC self-contained seed script |

## Interfaces / Contracts

```js
// ── Internal function signatures ──

// Parse .env file manually (no dotenv)
function parseEnv(path): { url: string, anonKey: string }

// Read & split file into CSV blocks by blank lines
function splitBlocks(raw): Array<{ header: string, rows: string[] }>

// Parse a single CSV line respecting double-quoted fields
function parseCsvRow(line): string[]  // returns array of field values

// Heal data: unescape \_ → _, repair truncated JSON → {}
// Fields array is from parseCsvRow, header defines column names
function healRow(header, fields): object  // returns { column: value }

// Determine if a block header is assets or hierarchy
function detectBlockType(header): 'assets' | 'hierarchy'

// Collect unique asset_type codes from all parsed asset rows
function extractAssetTypes(rows): string[]

// Upsert asset_types via REST API, return code → id map
async function upsertAssetTypes(codes, url, key): Promise<Map<string, number>>

// Insert assets in batch, return equipment_id → id map
async function insertAssets(rows, typeIdMap, url, key): Promise<Map<string, number>>

// Insert hierarchy rows using equipment_id → id lookup
async function insertHierarchy(rows, assetIdMap, url, key): Promise<number>

// ── REST API usage ──
// POST /rest/v1/asset_types
//   ?onConflict=code
//   Headers: apikey, Authorization: Bearer, Content-Type: application/json, Prefer: resolution=merge-duplicates, return=representation
//   Body: [{ code, description }]
// Returns: array of upserted rows with id
```

## Dry-Run Validation Logic

```
if (--dry-run):
  1. Parse blocks → log per type: "Assets: 4 blocks, 287 rows"
  2. Log distinct asset_type codes found
  3. Log first & last 3 parsed rows as objects (after healing)
  4. Log hierarchy: "Hierarchy: 3 blocks, 142 rows"
  5. Log any healing warnings (truncated JSON rows by line #)
  6. Exit code 0 — never touches DB
```

## Error Handling Strategy

| Layer | Strategy |
|-------|----------|
| File read | `throw` with descriptive message (missing file, permission) |
| CSV parse | Log row number on parse failure, `throw` to abort — data must be valid |
| JSON parse | Catch per-row: log `WARN: row X truncated JSON, using {}` + continue |
| Asset type upsert | Fail-fast if HTTP status ≥ 400 (abort script) |
| Asset insert | Fail-fast on batch error — re-run in dry-run is recovery path |
| Hierarchy insert | Fail-fast — but this is last step, error means partial state |

## Rollout

No migration or feature flags. Script is standalone. Run order:
1. `node scripts/seed_epicor.js --dry-run` — validate parsing
2. `pg_dump asset_types assets asset_hierarchy` — backup
3. `node scripts/seed_epicor.js` — full insert
4. Verify row counts match dry-run prediction
5. Re-run is idempotent via upserts

## Open Questions

- [ ] Confirm the `location_id` field maps to the `location` column on `assets` (schema shows `location`, data has values like `DOTACION`, `TOSTADO`)
- [ ] Should we also map `site` column? Data doesn't have a separate site field.

**What**: Implemented scripts/seed_epicor.js — one-shot Epicor data seed with CSV parsing, data healing, dry-run validation, and Supabase REST upserts.

observations.title: sdd/work-order-fsm-schema-phase-1/explore
observations.content:
**What**: Completed SDD Explore phase for work-order-fsm-schema-phase-1, analyzing current RxDB schema, Supabase table, replication handlers, asset FK relationship, and FSM options.
**Why**: The user requested exploration before committing to schema and FSM changes for an enterprise CMMS work order module.
**Where**: `src/lib/rxdb.js`, `src/hooks/useWorkOrders.js`, `sql/trigger-work_orders.sql`, `src/lib/supabaseClient.js`, `openspec/changes/work-order-fsm-schema-phase-1/explore.md`
**Learned**:
- The current `work_orders` RxDB schema is v1 with only 12 fields and a 4-value status enum; it's missing enterprise fields (wo_type, planned/actual hours, cost, approval, downtime, etc.).
- The replication pull handler for work_orders orders by `updated_at`, but the Supabase SQL definition has `_last_modified` instead. This is a likely latent bug that needs verification before design.
- `work_orders.equipment_id` references `assets.equipment_id`, not `assets.id`, creating a loose FK with no referential integrity. Normalizing to `asset_id` → `assets.id` is recommended.
- No FSM enforcement exists; status can change arbitrarily. Recommended transition matrix: open→{in_progress,cancelled}, in_progress→{paused,closed,cancelled}, paused→{in_progress,closed,cancelled}, closed/cancelled terminal.
- The `createPushHandler` field list for work_orders is missing any new fields and doesn't set `updated_at_ms` (unlike assets), creating inconsistency.
- Three approaches evaluated: (1) minimal app-level validation only, (2) full PostgreSQL trigger + audit table + RxDB mirror, (3) hybrid deferred. Recommendation is Approach 2 if review budget allows (~300-400 lines), else Approach 3 split.
- Risks: RxDB v1→v2 migration with Dexie can fail in StrictMode (code has recreate fallback but no migration function yet); replication stall if offline invalid states are rejected on push; equipment_id/asset_id ambiguity breaks UI lookups; status rename breaks downstream reporting.

4. **Audit table missing FK constraint**: Spec requires `work_order_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES work_orders(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`. Implementation omits FK.

6. **Push handler missing `updated_at_ms`**: Spec requires sending both `updated_at` (ISO string) and `updated_at_ms` (number). Implementation only sends `updated_at` as number.
7. **Push handler missing `updated_at` bump on conflict**: Design specifies bumping `updated_at` when marking `_conflict=true` to ensure pull ordering. Implementation omits the bump.

1. Commit the untracked `sql/migration-work_orders-v2.sql` and `openspec/changes/` directory to preserve SDD artifacts and DDL history.
2. Add `TO authenticated` to all RLS policies once auth context is available in Phase 2.
3. Add `ON DELETE CASCADE` FK to `work_order_status_history.work_order_id` for referential integrity.
4. Consider adding Vitest/Jest unit tests for `fsm.js` and migration logic to reduce reliance on slow Playwright e2e for algorithmic correctness.
5. Rename `preSave(..., false)` to `preUpdate` in code/comments once RxDB API permits, or update task wording to match actual API usage.

### Verdict

**PASS WITH WARNINGS**

The core database-layer upgrade is implemented correctly: RxDB v2 schema, FSM engine, migration strategy, PostgreSQL triggers, audit trail, RLS, and replication conflict handling are all present and build-clean. However, the implementation contains documented design deltas (`updated_at` schema, `asset_id` FK, audit FK, RLS role restriction) that deviate from the approved spec. PR 1 DDL is untracked in git. Phase 3 client-side unit/integration tests are missing, and the sole E2E test suite cannot execute due to a known auth infrastructure gap approved for Phase 2 resolution. No CRITICAL bugs were found.

observations.title: Sub-agentes SDD fallan por skills modificados entre sesiones
observations.content:
**What**: Sub-agentes SDD (sdd-apply, sdd-verify, sdd-archive) fallan con `ProviderModelNotFoundError` en esta sesión, pero funcionaron en sesión anterior después de cerrar y reabrir.

**Why**: Los archivos de skills en `~/.config/opencode/skills/` fueron modificados por agentes en la sesión anterior (probablemente por algún proceso de init o skill-registry). Al cerrar y abrir nueva sesión, los skills quedaron en estado inconsistente/corrupto. Esto afectó la resolución de modelos para sub-agentes en la sesión actual.

**Where**: `~/.config/opencode/skills/sdd-*/SKILL.md` y posiblemente archivos de `_shared/`.

**Learned**:
- Si sub-agentes SDD dejan de funcionar de repente, verificar si los archivos SKILL.md fueron modificados por otra sesión/agente.
- Workaround: usar `delegate(agent: "general", ...)` con el prompt completo del skill en vez de confiar en la resolución automática.
- Para recuperar: cerrar sesión, restaurar skills originales desde un backup o reinstalar el paquete gentle-ai skills, y reabrir opencode.
- No modificar archivos de skills del sistema durante una sesión a menos que sea estrictamente necesario.

observations.title: Explored OEE webhook edge function implementation
observations.content:
**What**: Completed sdd-explore phase for the OEE webhook Supabase Edge Function. Analyzed codebase structure, existing schemas, and identified exact fields and lookup patterns needed.
**Why**: Required to implement a webhook that receives equipment_id + sintoma from an external OEE app and creates a work_order in Supabase.
**Where**: `cmms-frontend-react/src/lib/rxdb.js`, `cmms-frontend-react/sql/migration-work_orders-v2.sql`, `cmms-frontend-react/openspec/changes/oee-webhook-module/exploration.md`
**Learned**:
- `assets.equipment_id` is the external lookup key but is NOT guaranteed unique in the current schema.
- `work_orders` v2 has 13 required fields; Supabase defaults cover most (status='pending', wo_type='corrective', numerics=0).
- The `updated_at` trigger auto-populates epoch ms on INSERT, so the edge function doesn't need to set it.
- RLS is enabled on `work_orders`; the edge function MUST use the Service Role Key to bypass policies.
- No existing `supabase/functions/` directory exists in the repo; this will be a greenfield addition.
- The FSM trigger only runs on UPDATE, so an INSERT with status='pending' will not be blocked.

observations.title: OEE Webhook architectural decisions
observations.content:
**What**: Defined 3 architectural decisions for the OEE webhook Edge Function
**Why**: User provided enterprise-grade security and collision-prevention guidelines before proceeding to Propose/Design
**Where**: Will affect supabase/functions/oee-trigger/index.ts
**Learned**:
1. equipment_id uniqueness: Assume unique (resolved during ETL), but defensively use .limit(1).maybeSingle() with 404 on not found.
2. ID format: UUID v4 standard for PK (no prefixes) to keep RxDB replication happy. Visual distinction goes in description field: "[OEE TRIGGER] Síntoma: <sintoma>"
3. OEE_SECRET_KEY: Managed in Supabase Dashboard secrets. Edge function reads Deno.env.get('OEE_SECRET_KEY'). Returns HTTP 401 if Authorization: Bearer header missing or invalid.

observations.title: Session summary: cmms-ibero
observations.content:
## Goal
Completar el ciclo SDD completo del Módulo de Integración OEE (Webhook) — una Supabase Edge Function `oee-trigger` que recibe alertas desde la App de Producción y genera Órdenes de Trabajo automáticamente.

observations.title: SDD Design: pm-engine-cron-calendar
observations.content:
**View Definition**
```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW pm_due_calendar AS
SELECT
  ps.id AS schedule_id,
  ps.asset_id,
  a.equipment_id AS asset_name,
  jp.code AS job_plan_title,
  ps.next_target_date AS projected_date,
  'PM'::text AS wo_type,
  jp.intervention_type,
  ps.time_frequency_days,
  ps.parent_schedule_id,
  CASE WHEN ps.next_target_date <= CURRENT_DATE THEN 'OVERDUE' ELSE 'PENDING' END AS status
FROM pm_schedules ps
JOIN assets a ON a.id = ps.asset_id
JOIN job_plans jp ON jp.id = ps.job_plan_id
WHERE ps.next_target_date IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY ps.next_target_date ASC;
```

observations.title: SDD Proposal: epicor-outbox-pattern
observations.content:
**What**: Implementar el Patrón Outbox (Transactional Outbox) para el pipeline de salida CMMS → Epicor, garantizando Guaranteed Delivery.

**Why**: Desacoplar el CMMS de la disponibilidad de Epicor. El sistema nunca habla directamente con el ERP. En su lugar, escribe a una tabla de cola (epicor_outbox) y un adaptador futuro se encarga del envío asíncrono. Esto protege contra caídas de red, timeouts, y cambios de protocolo.

**Scope**:
- Migración: `20260526000001_create_epicor_outbox.sql` — tabla + índices + trigger
- Trigger: `trg_enqueue_material_request` en material_requests (INSERT → epicor_outbox)
- Test: pgTAP que valida inserción automática en outbox
- Openspec: artifacts en openspec/changes/epicor-outbox-pattern/

**Approach**:
1. Crear tabla epicor_outbox con CHECK states y exponential backoff
2. Crear trigger AFTER INSERT en material_requests que inyecta en cola
3. Test: seed → INSERT material_request → verificar outbox
4. Documentar en openspec + engram

observations.title: SDD Spec: epicor-outbox-pattern
observations.content:
**Requirements**

R1 — Tabla epicor_outbox con campos: id (UUID PK), event_type (TEXT), payload (JSONB), status (TEXT DEFAULT 'PENDING'), retry_count (INT DEFAULT 0), next_retry_at (TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()), last_error (TEXT), created_at (TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()), processed_at (TIMESTAMPTZ)

R2 — CHECK constraint status IN ('PENDING', 'PROCESSING', 'SENT', 'FAILED')

R3 — Índice compuesto en (status, next_retry_at) para polling eficiente del adaptador

R4 — Trigger trg_enqueue_material_request AFTER INSERT ON material_requests FOR EACH ROW. Debe capturar: id, work_order_id, part_num, requested_qty, warehouse_code, event_type = 'MATERIAL_REQUEST_CREATE'

R5 — next_retry_at debe iniciar en NOW() para que el adaptador lo procese inmediatamente

**Scenarios**
1. INSERT en material_requests → registro en epicor_outbox con status PENDING
2. payload contiene todos los campos vitales
3. next_retry_at = NOW() (listo para procesar)

observations.title: SDD Design: epicor-outbox-pattern
observations.content:
**Table Definition**
```sql
CREATE TABLE epicor_outbox (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  event_type TEXT NOT NULL,
  payload JSONB NOT NULL,
  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'PENDING',
  retry_count INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  next_retry_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  last_error TEXT,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  processed_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  CONSTRAINT epicor_outbox_status_check CHECK (status IN ('PENDING', 'PROCESSING', 'SENT', 'FAILED'))
);
CREATE INDEX idx_epicor_outbox_poll ON epicor_outbox (status, next_retry_at);
```

**Trigger Function**
```sql
CREATE FUNCTION enqueue_material_request()
RETURNS TRIGGER LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER AS $$
BEGIN
  INSERT INTO epicor_outbox (event_type, payload)
  VALUES (
    'MATERIAL_REQUEST_CREATE',
    jsonb_build_object(
      'material_request_id', NEW.id,
      'work_order_id', NEW.work_order_id,
      'part_num', NEW.part_num,
      'requested_qty', NEW.requested_qty,
      'line_desc', NEW.line_desc
    )
  );
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;
CREATE TRIGGER trg_enqueue_material_request
  AFTER INSERT ON material_requests
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION enqueue_material_request();
```

**Migration**: `20260526000001_create_epicor_outbox.sql`

**Test**: `supabase/tests/database/epicor_outbox_test.sql` — seed → INSERT → verificar cola

**Openspec**: openspec/changes/epicor-outbox-pattern/{proposal,spec,design,tasks,verify}.md

observations.title: Session summary: cmms-ibero
observations.content:
## Goal
Cerrar el ciclo completo del PM Engine (pg_cron + pm_due_calendar), implementar Epicor Outbox Pattern, arreglar bugs en migraciones y tests, y discutir la estrategia de ARQUITECTURA para competir con plataformas clase mundial (IBM Maximo, SAP PM).

## Instructions
- **Documentar todo en Engram + openspec** — modo híbrido. Esta sesión se documentó en ambos formatos.
- **Dejar frontend para el final** — priorizar backend, base de datos, integraciones y modelos.
- **No escribir código outbound a Epicor** hasta tener definido el protocolo con TI.
- **Siempre TDD** — test pgTAP antes de la migración.
- **Auto mode en SDD** — no preguntar, ejecutar y reportar.

## Discoveries
- **Bug cascade**: 3 bugs iniciales (dc.id, status column, asset_type FK) escondían 6 bugs relacionados (UUID vs TEXT, audit trigger, enum lifecycle_phase, storerooms.code, spare_parts FK, type mismatches). Arreglar la raíz destapó todo.
- **pgTAP quirks**: COUNT(*) retorna bigint, no integer. results_eq requires tipos exactos. BEFORE INSERT triggers no pueden distinguir valor explícito de DEFAULT. SAVEPOINT/ROLLBACK confunde el contador interno de finish().
- **THINK-ANYWHERE paper**: No aplica a modelos predictivos industriales (Weibull, ROP, MTBF). El parallel correcto es nuestro CBM Trigger. El paper sirve para NL2SQL futuro, no para el core del CMMS.
- **3 ciegos de Tora**: (1) Wrench Time requiere labor_reporting, no solo status_history. (2) Safety/LOTO/certificaciones deben diseñarse desde ahora aunque se implementen después. (3) Almacén necesita conectar stock con dispatch (qty_on_hand, reorder_point).
- **Epicor Outbox**: El trigger en material_requests funciona (9/9 tests). El adaptador outbound se diseña cuando TI defina protocolo.

## Accomplished

observations.title: Fix crítico: Client-Driven clock en lugar de triggers server-side
observations.content:
**What**: Eliminar trigger de auto-creación/cierre de labor_records en PostgreSQL. La lógica de clock-in/out debe vivir en el frontend (useLaborRecords.js) como dos transacciones atómicas en RxDB: (1) cambiar WO a INPRG, (2) crear labor_record con start_time y activity_code. El servidor solo valida: trigger defensivo trg_validate_labor_fsm que verifica que la WO esté en INPRG cuando recibe un labor_record activo.
**Why**: En offline-first, si el trigger server-side crea labor_records al detectar INPRG, y RxDB ya creó uno localmente offline, al sincronizar se genera un DUPLICATE FANTASMA. Además el trigger no sabe qué técnico inició la sesión.
**Where**: openspec/changes/labor-reporting/design.md, migración labor_records.sql, useLaborRecords.js
**Learned**: En offline-first, el cliente es el rey de la creación, el servidor es la bóveda de validación. Los triggers server-side que crean datos basados en estados transicionales son una mina terrestre en RxDB.

observations.title: sdd/labor-reporting/explore
observations.content:
## Exploration: Labor Reporting / Time Tracking

### Current State

**The codebase has ZERO labor tracking today.** No clock-in/out, no time entries, no technician hours against work orders. The mechanic UI (Phase 2 — Execution) allows lifecycle transitions (APPROVED→INPRG→COMP→CLOSED) and technical notes, but does not capture who worked how long on what.

**Relevant existing schema:**
- **user_profiles** — id (UUID FK auth.users), full_name (TEXT), role (TEXT), erp_employee_num (TEXT UNIQUE). Technician identity but NO labor/qualification data.
- **work_orders** — has `planned_hours` (NUMERIC) and `actual_hours` (NUMERIC) as aggregate fields, plus `actual_start_at` / `completed_at` timestamps. Not tied to individual technicians.
- **job_plans** — has `estimated_hours` per plan.

**Existing mechanic UI flow:** MechanicDashboard → WorkOrderList → WorkOrderDrawer (read-only detail + notes form + action buttons). No labor concept exists anywhere.

**FSM lifecycle touch points:** APPROVED→INPRG (ideal clock-in), INPRG→COMP (ideal clock-out), COMP→CLOSED (auto-sum hours).

### Affected Areas

- **`supabase/migrations/202605<next>_labor_records.sql`** — NEW: labor_records table, RLS, FSM triggers
- **`src/lib/rxdb.js`** — MODIFY: add labor_records collection + replication
- **`src/lib/adapters/laborAdapter.js`** — NEW: adapter pattern
- **`src/hooks/useLaborRecords.js`** — NEW: RxDB hook
- **`src/components/mechanic/LaborClockWidget.jsx`** — NEW: clock-in/out UI
- **`src/components/mechanic/WorkOrderDrawer.jsx`** — MODIFY: add clock widget, labor validation
- **`src/components/mechanic/WorkOrderActions.jsx`** — MODIFY: disable COMP if no clock-in
- **`supabase/tests/database/labor_records_test.sql`** — NEW: pgTAP tests

### Approaches

#### Approach 1: Simple labor_records table (manual hours entry)
Schema: labor_records(id, work_order_id, technician_id, hours_worked, date_logged, notes). No clock-in/out.
- **Pros**: Simplest, fast, no FSM coupling, easy offline
- **Cons**: Self-reported hours (inaccurate), no real Wrench Time, no audit trail
- **Effort**: Low (~50 SQL + 80 RxDB + 150 UI + 100 tests)

#### Approach 2: Clock-in/out with timestamps (RECOMMENDED)
Schema: labor_records(id, work_order_id, technician_id, clock_in_at, clock_out_at, hours_worked GENERATED, pause_minutes, notes). Auto clock-in on APPROVED→INPRG, auto clock-out on INPRG→COMP.
- **Pros**: Accurate time capture, natural FSM integration, Wrench Time ready, supports multi-technician, audit trail
- **Cons**: More complex FSM coupling, edge cases (forgot clock-in, offline), needs "running clock" awareness
- **Effort**: Medium (~80 SQL + 120 RxDB + 300 UI + 200 tests)

#### Approach 3: Full labor reporting (clock-in/out + crafts + cost + shifts)
Adds crafts table, technician_crafts table, shift management, hourly cost rates, geolocation, Wrench Time analytics views.
- **Pros**: Complete solution, future-proof, cost tracking, regulatory compliance
- **Cons**: Over-engineered for Phase 1, high effort, crafts admin UI needed, security concerns with cost data
- **Effort**: High (~200 SQL + 200 RxDB + 600 UI + 350 tests)

### Recommendation
**Approach 2 — Clock-in/out with timestamps.** Pragmatic middle ground. Gives accurate Wrench Time data, integrates with existing FSM, supports offline-first, and leaves a clean path to Approach 3 for Phase 2 (add crafts, costs, shifts later).

### Risks
- Forgot to clock in/out → allow manual fallback + admin override
- Offline with wrong device time → store device_timestamp, sync with server
- Multi-day WO → support pause/resume or multiple clock sessions (auto-sum)
- Multi-technician on same WO → each gets own labor_record row
- FSM rejection during network issues → RxDB conflict flag pattern

### Ready for Proposal
**Yes.** Confirm single-site, no crafts in Phase 1, and multi-day WO strategy with the user.

observations.title: sdd/labor-reporting/proposal
observations.content:
# Proposal: Labor Reporting / Time Tracking

## Intent

Enable mechanics to clock in/out against work orders with activity codes, capturing accurate wrench-time data for future productivity analysis. Replaces manual hours estimation with real clock data.

## Scope

### In Scope
- `labor_records` table (Supabase migration + RLS + audit trigger)
- RxDB `labor_records` collection + push/pull replication + hook + adapter
- Clock-in/out widget in WorkOrderDrawer with activity code selector
- FSM auto clock-in on APPROVED→INPRG, auto clock-out on INPRG→COMP
- COMP transition blocked if no active clock session
- Multiple clock sessions per WO (no pause/resume)
- Re-add `actual_hours` to `work_orders` (auto-sum on COMP→CLOSED)
- Offline-first via RxDB

### Out of Scope
- Crafts/qualifications tables (Phase 2)
- GPS/geolocation (Phase 2)
- Cost rates / payroll integration (Phase 2+)
- Labor dashboards / Wrench Time analytics (Phase 2 — raw data only)

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities
- `labor-records-database`: labor_records table, CHECK constraint on activity_code, RLS, FSM integration triggers, audit trail
- `labor-records-rxdb`: RxDB collection schema, replication handlers, `useLaborRecords` hook, `laborAdapter`
- `labor-clock-widget`: ClockWidget component with activity code selector inside WorkOrderDrawer

### Modified Capabilities
- `mechanic-work-order-execution`: Drawer includes clock widget, COMP validation checks for open clock session

## Approach

Clock-in/out with **multiple independent sessions** per WO (no pause/resume). Each session is a `labor_records` row with `start_time`, nullable `end_time`, and required `activity_code`. Hours are `GENERATED ALWAYS AS` — no manual entry.

| Event | Action |
|-------|--------|
| APPROVED→INPRG | Auto-create DIRECT_WORK session if none active |
| INPRG→COMP | Set `end_time = NOW()` on active session |
| COMP→CLOSED | SUM all labor_records → `work_orders.actual_hours` |
| Manual clock-in | Select activity code → insert with `start_time = NOW()` |
| Manual clock-out | Set `end_time = NOW()` on the active record |

## Affected Areas

| Area | Impact | Detail |
|------|--------|--------|
| `supabase/migrations/202605<next>_labor_records.sql` | NEW | labor_records table, updated_at trigger, RLS, FSM trigger integration, ALTER work_orders ADD actual_hours |
| `supabase/tests/database/labor_records_test.sql` | NEW | pgTAP tests for schema, RLS, FSM triggers |
| `src/lib/rxdb.js` | MODIFY | Add labor_records schema + collection + replication handlers to `addCollections()` and `startAllReplications()` |
| `src/lib/adapters/laborAdapter.js` | NEW | RxDB→ViewModel mapping (same pattern as workOrderAdapter) |
| `src/hooks/useLaborRecords.js` | NEW | RxDB hook with subscription (same pattern as useWorkOrders) |
| `src/components/mechanic/LaborClockWidget.jsx` | NEW | Clock-in/out button + activity code selector |
| `src/pages/MechanicDashboard.jsx` | MODIFY | Wire `useLaborRecords` hook, pass labor state to drawer |
| `src/components/mechanic/WorkOrderDrawer.jsx` | MODIFY | Add clock widget section, labor session display |
| `src/components/mechanic/WorkOrderActions.jsx` | MODIFY | Accept `hasActiveClock` prop, disable COMP if no clock |

## Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|------|------------|------------|
| Mechanic forgets clock-in | Medium | Allow manual session creation as fallback within drawer |
| Offline clock with wrong device time | Low | Store `device_timestamp`; reconcile with server on sync |
| Multi-day WO | Low | Multiple sessions auto-summed on COMP→CLOSED |
| Concurrent edits on same labor_record | Low | Each session is own row; no conflict expected |

## Rollback Plan

1. Remove labor_records collection from `startAllReplications()`
2. Drop `labor_records` table via migration
3. Remove `actual_hours` column if it was added by migration
4. Revert Drawer/Actions/MechanicDashboard to previous versions

## Dependencies

None — `labor_records` references existing `work_orders(id)` (TEXT) and `user_profiles(id)` (UUID).

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Mechanic can clock in with activity code from WO drawer
- [ ] COMP transition is blocked when no active clock session exists
- [ ] Offline clock-in/out syncs when connectivity returns
- [ ] FSM trigger creates labor_record on APPROVED→INPRG (auto DIRECT_WORK)
- [ ] COMP→CLOSED sums all labor_records.hours_worked → work_orders.actual_hours
- [ ] RLS: TECHNICIAN can CRUD own records, PLANNER/ADMIN can see all
- [ ] All data survives page reload (RxDB persistence + sync)

observations.title: sdd/labor-reporting/design
observations.content:
# Design: Labor Reporting / Time Tracking (CORRECTED - Client-Driven)

## Architecture
Three-layer: **RxDB client orchestrates** (creates labor_records atomically with WO status), **DB validates** (defensive triggers, no auto-creation), **ClockWidget** delivers mechanic UI.

## Key Decision: Client-Driven Clock
REJECTED: DB BEFORE UPDATE trigger auto-creates labor_record on INPRG (causes DUPLICATE FANTASMA on offline sync, doesn't know technician)
CHOSEN: RxDB client creates labor_records atomically with WO status change. Server only VALIDATES.

## Data Flow
Clock-in: ClockWidget → useLaborRecords.clockIn() → RxDB: (1) WO→INPRG, (2) INSERT labor_record → sync → Supabase validates
Clock-out: ClockWidget → useLaborRecords.clockOut() → RxDB: (1) UPDATE labor_record end_time, (2) WO→COMP if no active → sync → validates
COMP→CLOSED: Supabase trigger SUMs labor_records → work_orders.actual_hours
Offline: RxDB writes locally → timer runs instantly → sync when online → no duplicates

## New files: migration, pgTAP tests, laborAdapter.js, useLaborRecords.js, LaborClockWidget.jsx
## Modified: WorkOrderDrawer.jsx, WorkOrderActions.jsx, MechanicDashboard.jsx, rxdb.js

## Defensive DB Triggers
- trg_validate_labor_fsm(): BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE ON labor_records — verify WO is INPRG for active sessions, verify technician ownership
- trg_labor_sum_hours(): BEFORE UPDATE ON work_orders — COMP→CLOSED SUM actual_hours
- NO auto-create triggers anywhere

observations.title: sdd/safety-permits/explore
observations.content:
**What**: Complete exploration of the Safety & Permits (HSE) module for the CMMS. Analyzed current codebase, existing patterns (FSM triggers, RLS, audit trail, pgTAP tests), and designed schema approaches for 6 sub-modules: PTW, LOTO, Incidents, Hazards, Risk Assessment, MOC.

**Why**: The CMMS has zero safety/HSE tables despite the codebase already acknowledging permit-related concepts (WAIT_PERMIT activity_code in labor_records, PERMIT block_reason in work_orders). This exploration evaluates how to add comprehensive HSE capabilities incrementally.

**Where**: 
- `openspec/changes/safety-permits/exploration.md` — Full exploration document
- Existing references affected: `work_orders` (permit_id FK), `labor_records` (WAIT_PERMIT concept), `user_profiles` (new SAFETY_OFFICER role needed), `block_reason` ENUM (already has PERMIT)
- Future migrations: `*_safety_permit_types.sql`, `*_safety_ptw_loto.sql`, `*_safety_incidents.sql`, `*_safety_hazards_risk.sql`, `*_safety_moc.sql`

**Learned**:
1. The existing FSM trigger pattern (BEFORE UPDATE, forward-only linear transitions) maps perfectly to permit lifecycle states (DRAFT→SUBMITTED→REVIEW→APPROVED→ACTIVE→COMPLETED/CANCELLED/REJECTED/EXPIRED)
2. Approval chain pattern designed for PTW (permit_approvals table with sequential levels) is directly reusable for MOC reviews
3. Risk assessment needs a GENERATED risk_level column based on likelihood × severity (5×5 matrix)
4. Three approaches evaluated: Minimal v1 (PTW+LOTO only), Complete HSE (all 6 at once), Phased HSE (PTW first, then incidents+hazards+risk, then MOC)
5. Recommendation: Phased HSE starting with PTW+LOTO, using UUID PKs everywhere to anticipate future Phase 2/3 FK relationships
6. New SAFETY_OFFICER and HSE_MANAGER roles needed alongside existing ADMIN/PLANNER/TECHNICIAN/STOREKEEPER

# Proposal: Safety & Permits — Phase 1 (PTW + LOTO)

## Intent

CMMS references permits (`WAIT_PERMIT`, `PERMIT` block_reason) but has zero HSE tables. Add Permit to Work and Lockout/Tagout — the highest-value safety entry point — so planners issue, approve, and track work permits with isolation procedures.

## Scope

### In Scope
- 5 tables: `permit_types`, `work_permits`, `permit_tasks`, `lockout_tagout`, `tagout_devices`
- `SAFETY_OFFICER` role added to `user_profiles` CHECK
- ENUMs: `permit_status` (7 states), `device_type` (LOCK/TAG/HASPS/CHAIN)
- FSM trigger on `permit_status` (REQUESTED→APPROVED→ACTIVE→COMPLETED|REJECTED|CANCELLED|EXPIRED)
- RLS per role, audit triggers (reuse existing), pgTAP tests, Spanish COMMENTS

### Out of Scope
- Incidents, hazards, risk, MOC (Phase 2/3)
- Frontend, notifications, RxDB/offline

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities
- `permit-to-work`: PTW lifecycle, permit types catalog, tasks/precautions, isolation & gas test tracking
- `lockout-tagout`: LOTO procedures linked to permits/WOs, device tracking, status workflow (PLANNED→LOCKED→VERIFIED→REMOVED)

### Modified Capabilities
- `auth-rbac`: Add SAFETY_OFFICER to role matrix

## Approach

Phase 1 of Phased HSE. Schema-only. Follow existing patterns: UUID PKs, TIMESTAMPTZ, generic audit trigger, forward-only FSM, RLS via `get_user_role()`, pgTAP BEGIN/ROLLBACK. Permits FK to work_orders/assets. LOTO FK to permits or WOs.

## Affected Areas

| Area | Impact |
|------|--------|
| `supabase/migrations/*_safety_permit_types.sql` | New |
| `supabase/migrations/*_safety_ptw_loto.sql` | New |
| `supabase/migrations/*_add_safety_officer_role.sql` | New |
| `supabase/tests/database/safety_ptw_loto_test.sql` | New |
| `openspec/specs/permit-to-work/spec.md` | New |
| `openspec/specs/lockout-tagout/spec.md` | New |

## Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|------|------------|------------|
| SAFETY_OFFICER needs wider RBAC changes | High | ADMIN approver fallback; role migration isolated |
| Permit FSM too simple for real-world | Med | 7 states; HOLD/SUSPENDED via ENUM later |
| LOTO device inventory complexity | Low | AVAILABLE/IN_USE/LOST/DAMAGED only |

## Rollback Plan

Drop migrations in reverse order (role, ptw_loto, permit_types). Independent — no cross-migration data deps. Data loss limited to safety tables.

## Dependencies

- `work_orders`, `assets`, `user_profiles` (all exist)

## Success Criteria

- [ ] PLANNER creates work permit linked to a WO
- [ ] SAFETY_OFFICER approves/rejects; unauthorized roles cannot
- [ ] FSM enforces valid forward-only transitions
- [ ] LOTO procedure created, locked, verified, removed
- [ ] RLS restricts access by role on all tables
- [ ] All pgTAP tests pass

observations.title: sdd/safety-permits/spec
observations.content:
# SDD Spec: safety-permits

## permit-to-work — Specification

### Purpose
Define the Permit to Work (PTW) system for hazardous work control. Manages permit requests, approval, activation, and closure with isolation and gas test tracking.

### Tables

**permit_types**: id UUID PK, code TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL, name TEXT NOT NULL, description TEXT, requires_isolation BOOLEAN DEFAULT false, requires_gas_test BOOLEAN DEFAULT false, validity_hours INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (>0), created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(). Seeded: HOT_WORK, COLD_WORK, CONFINED_SPACE, HEIGHT_WORK, EXCAVATION, ELECTRICAL, RADIATION.

**work_permits**: id UUID PK, permit_type_id UUID FK→permit_types NOT NULL, work_order_id UUID FK→work_orders, asset_id UUID FK→assets, permit_status permit_status DEFAULT 'REQUESTED', requested_by UUID FK→user_profiles, approved_by UUID FK→user_profiles nullable, issued_at TIMESTAMPTZ, expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ CHECK(>issued_at), completed_at TIMESTAMPTZ, isolation_required BOOLEAN DEFAULT false, gas_test_required BOOLEAN DEFAULT false, gas_test_result TEXT CHECK(IN('PASS','FAIL',NULL)), description TEXT NOT NULL, location TEXT, created_at/updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ.

**permit_tasks**: id UUID PK, work_permit_id UUID FK→work_permits ON DELETE CASCADE NOT NULL, step_sequence INTEGER CHECK(>0) NOT NULL, task_description TEXT NOT NULL, is_precaution BOOLEAN DEFAULT false, completed BOOLEAN DEFAULT false, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ.

### FSM: permit_status (7 states)
REQUESTED → APPROVED → ACTIVE → COMPLETED (terminal). REQUESTED also→CANCELLED, REJECTED. APPROVED also→CANCELLED, EXPIRED. ACTIVE also→EXPIRED. Forward-only trigger; auto-expire ACTIVE where expires_at < NOW().

### RLS
ADMIN|SAFETY_OFFICER: ALL. PLANNER: SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE. TECHNICIAN: SELECT. Via get_user_role().

### Audit
audit_trigger_func() on all tables via BEFORE UPDATE trigger.

### Scenarios
- SAFETY_OFFICER completes full lifecycle: INSERT REQUESTED → UPDATE APPROVED → ACTIVE → COMPLETED; backward transitions rejected.
- FSM rejects REQUESTED→COMPLETED jump: trigger raises exception.
- Gas test required before ACTIVE: trigger blocks when gas_test_required=true AND gas_test_result IS NULL.
- Permit auto-expires: ACTIVE permit with expires_at < NOW() transitions to EXPIRED on any UPDATE.
- Tasks cascade on permit DELETE: CASCADE removes all permit_tasks.
- TECHNICIAN read-only: SELECT returns rows, INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE rejected by RLS.

## lockout-tagout — Specification

### Purpose
Define LOTO for energy isolation. Tracks isolation lifecycle from planning through verified removal.

### Tables

**lockout_tagout**: id UUID PK, work_permit_id UUID FK→work_permits, work_order_id UUID FK→work_orders, asset_id UUID FK→assets, loto_status loto_status DEFAULT 'PLANNED', description TEXT NOT NULL, locked_by UUID FK→user_profiles, locked_at TIMESTAMPTZ, verified_by UUID FK→user_profiles, verified_at TIMESTAMPTZ CHECK(≥locked_at), removed_by UUID FK→user_profiles, removed_at TIMESTAMPTZ CHECK(≥verified_at), created_at/updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ.

**tagout_devices**: id UUID PK, lockout_tagout_id UUID FK→lockout_tagout ON DELETE CASCADE NOT NULL, device_type device_type NOT NULL, device_id TEXT NOT NULL, device_label TEXT.

### FSM: loto_status (4 states)
PLANNED → LOCKED → VERIFIED → REMOVED. Forward-only BEFORE UPDATE trigger.

### ENUMs
loto_status: PLANNED, LOCKED, VERIFIED, REMOVED.
device_type: LOCK, TAG, HASPS, CHAIN.

### RLS
ADMIN|SAFETY_OFFICER: ALL. PLANNER: SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE. TECHNICIAN: SELECT.

### Audit
audit_trigger_func() on both tables.

### Scenarios
- SAFETY_OFFICER completes LOTO: PLANNED→LOCKED→VERIFIED→REMOVED; backward transitions rejected.
- FSM rejects LOCKED→REMOVED skip: VERIFIED required first.
- Two-person rule: verified_by must differ from locked_by.
- Multiple devices per procedure: 3 devices (2 locks, 1 tag) all cascade on procedure delete.
- Device type ENUM rejects invalid values.
- PLANNER creates LOTO but cannot DELETE.
- At least one of work_permit_id or work_order_id SHOULD be set.

**Learned**:
1. PTW FSM: trigger-based BEFORE UPDATE, 7 states (REQUESTED→APPROVED→ACTIVE→COMPLETED + REJECTED/CANCELLED/EXPIRED terminals).
2. LOTO FSM: 4 states PLANNED→LOCKED→VERIFIED→REMOVED. Two-person rule (`verified_by != locked_by`) in trigger.

5. No auto-creation triggers — same client-driven philosophy as labor-reporting.
6. Single migration file (not three) — all new tables, no data dependencies.

**What**: Phase 2 (pgTAP tests) completed — comprehensive test suite for PTW + LOTO schema

**Why**: User requested Phase 2 of safety-permits change: pgTAP tests covering schema, PTW FSM, LOTO FSM, RLS, and cascade behaviors

**Where**:

**Learned**:
- PostgreSQL triggers fire in alphabetical order by trigger name: trg_permit_auto_expiry ('p') fires before trg_validate_permit_fsm ('v'), which is critical for auto-expiry logic to work correctly
- Auto-expiry trigger checks OLD.expires_at — to test it, need TWO updates: first set expires_at to past (no auto-expiry because OLD value is still future), then a second update triggers the expiry (OLD is now past)
- RLS INSERT violations raise SQLSTATE '23514' (check_violation) from WITH CHECK policies
- RLS UPDATE/DELETE violations silently affect 0 rows via USING policies (no exception raised)
- Test users must exist in BOTH auth.users AND user_profiles for get_user_role() to work with auth.uid()
- FK columns to work_orders and assets are TEXT because those tables use TEXT primary keys
- CHECK constraint `chk_expires_after_issued` requires expires_at > issued_at, so test must set both when manipulating dates

observations.content:
**What**: Descubierto que work_orders.id y assets.id son de tipo TEXT (no UUID) en el esquema actual del proyecto

**Why**: Al implementar las FKs de safety-permits (work_permits.work_order_id, lockout_tagout.asset_id), se necesitaba el tipo correcto para las REFERENCES

**Where**: `supabase/migrations/20260520000002_work_orders_iso14224.sql` línea 20, `supabase/migrations/20260501000000_bootstrap_assets.sql` línea 22

**Learned**: 
- `work_orders.id TEXT PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()::text` — se genera UUID pero se almacena como TEXT
- `assets.id TEXT PRIMARY KEY` — sin default, se inserta desde Epicor
- Esto significa que cualquier FK hacia work_orders o assets debe ser TEXT, no UUID
- El diseño de safety-permits tenía esto como pregunta abierta ("Confirm work_permits.work_order_id FK matches TEXT type of work_orders.id") — ahora está resuelto: sí es TEXT
- labor_records ya lo usa correctamente: `work_order_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES work_orders(id)`

observations.title: Role CHECK debe incluir STOREKEEPER al agregar SAFETY_OFFICER
observations.content:
**What**: Al modificar user_profiles role CHECK para agregar SAFETY_OFFICER, el diseño original omitió STOREKEEPER pero debe incluirse

**Why**: STOREKEEPER es un rol existente usado en RLS policies de work_orders (`get_user_role() IN ('PLANNER', 'TECHNICIAN', 'STOREKEEPER')`). Excluirlo rompería datos existentes.

**Where**: `supabase/migrations/20260527000001_safety_permits.sql` línea 42-43, RLS en `20260520000002_work_orders_iso14224.sql` línea 174

**Learned**: La constraint final debe ser: `CHECK (role IN ('TECHNICIAN','PLANNER','ADMIN','STOREKEEPER','SAFETY_OFFICER'))`. El diseño en `openspec/changes/safety-permits/design.md` línea 56 menciona solo 4 roles sin STOREKEEPER. Siempre verificar todas las RLS policies existentes para detectar roles en uso.

observations.title: Decisiones arquitectónicas GEMA Competency Engine v1
observations.content:
**What**: Decisiones congeladas para el GEMA Competency Engine v1.
**Why**: Respuestas del usuario a las 5 preguntas bloqueantes de la exploración.
**Decisions**:
1. Approach 3 (GEMA Dynamic Engine) — CONFIRMADO 100%
2. Estructura evidencia: work_order_id, technician_id, asset_id, modulo_gema, nivel_evaluado, item_evaluado, status (PASS/FAIL). MVP manual por Planner, v2 desde checklists.
3. 8 módulos tecnológicos: M-PACK, M-TRAN, M-ELEC, M-REFR, M-VAPO (fusionado con M-CAL), M-PUMP, M-TÉRM, M-INFR
4. Niveles 1 y 5: trigger manual (induccion_modulo_completada boolean, autor_estandar boolean). Motor calcula niveles 2,3,4 automáticamente.
5. Candado: SOFT-LOCK con warning amarillo. Hard-lock diferido a v3 (con 3+ meses de histórico).
**Learned**: La fusión M-VAPO+M-CAL evita duplicar perfiles. M-PUMP y M-TÉRM son críticos para planta de chocolate (bombas lobulares, Cavemill). Soft-lock evita congelar operación mientras la matriz nace en ceros.

observations.title: sdd/competency-engine/explore
observations.content:
**What**: Exploration completa del GEMA Competency Engine. Diseño de 6 tablas (skills, proficiency_levels, technician_skills, skill_requirements, technician_skill_evidence, skill_gap_alerts) con cálculo dinámico de niveles desde checklists (Bloques A/B/C), candado de asignación, evidencia trazable y gap analysis predictivo.

**Why**: Las matrices de competencias tradicionales (Maximo HSE, SAP PM) son estáticas, subjetivas y desconectadas de las OTs. Este diseño las hace objetivas, dinámicas y predictivas — el nivel emerge del trabajo real en checklists.

**Where**: 
- `supabase/migrations/202605<next>_competency_engine.sql` — Tablas: skills, proficiency_levels, technician_skills, skill_requirements, technician_skill_evidence, skill_gap_alerts. Trigger de recálculo dinámico al completar checklist. Candado de asignación en job_plans/skill_requirements.
- `supabase/tests/database/competency_engine_test.sql` — pgTAP tests
- `src/lib/rxdb.js` — Modify para colecciones de skills/technician_skills
- `src/hooks/useCompetencyEngine.js` — NEW hook RxDB
- `src/components/planner/SkillGapDashboard.jsx` — NEW dashboard de gaps
- `src/components/planner/TechnicianSkillMatrix.jsx` — NEW matriz visual
- `src/components/mechanic/WorkOrderDrawer.jsx` — Modify para candado de asignación

**Architecture**:
- Tablas: skills (M-PACK, M-TRAN, M-ELEC, M-REFR, M-VAPO, M-CAL), proficiency_levels (1-5 con triggers), technician_skills (nivel calculado), skill_requirements (nivel mínimo por job_plan), technician_skill_evidence (checklists que contribuyeron), skill_gap_alerts (predictivo)
- Niveles: 1=Awareness (leyó LUPs), 2=Assisted (Bloque A), 3=Independent (Bloque B 5+ WOs), 4=Specialist (Bloque C), 5=Master (crea SOPs)
- Trigger recálculo: AFTER INSERT/UPDATE en technician_skill_evidence → recalcula technician_skills.current_level
- Candado: BEFORE UPDATE en work_orders (APPROVED→INPRG) verifica technician_skills.level >= skill_requirements.minimum_level
- Gap analysis: Función SQL que cruza pm_schedules con skill_requirements para predecir bottlenecks

**Approaches**:
1. technician_crafts estática — asignar oficio al técnico (Electricista, Mecánico, etc). Simple pero no es evidencia real de competencia.
2. Skills matrix manual — supervisor asigna niveles. El enfoque estándar en Maximo/SAP. Subjetivo, estático, requiere admin manual.
3. GEMA Dynamic Engine ⭐ — niveles calculados desde checklists. Objetivo, dinámico, predictivo, sin admin.

**Learned**: 
1. CRÍTICO: No existen tablas de checklists en el código actual. Las checklists con bloques A/B/C son un concepto NUEVO que necesita su propia implementación. El competency engine debe diseñarse para RECIBIR resultados de checklists (no definirlos), manteniendo separación de responsabilidades.
2. CRÍTICO: No existen módulos tecnológicos (M-PACK, M-TRAN, etc.) en assets. assets tiene asset_type pero sin relación a módulo tecnológico. Se necesita crear la tabla technological_modules y agregar module_id a assets.
3. labor_records es la única conexión existente entre technician y work_order (technician_id + work_order_id) — permite trazar technician → WO → asset → module.
4. work_orders tiene job_plan_id FK — permite agregar skill_requirements a job_plans sin cambios de schema en work_orders.
5. El patrón de FSM triggers (BEFORE UPDATE, forward-only) establecido en work_orders y permisos se reutiliza para el candado de asignación.
6. El user_profiles actual permite roles (TECHNICIAN, PLANNER, ADMIN, STOREKEEPER, SAFETY_OFFICER) — no necesita cambios de rol para competency engine.
7. El patrón de diseño de labor-reporting (client-driven con RxDB, server valida) debe replicarse aquí.
