observations.content:
## Goal
Implement "pm-schedule-copy" change — two SECURITY DEFINER functions to copy PM schedules between assets (`copy_pm_schedules_to_asset`) and between job plans (`copy_pm_schedules_to_plan`), following Strict TDD mode.

## Instructions
- Write pgTAP tests FIRST, then migration code
- Match existing patterns from `dup_job_plan` and `copy_job_plan_test`
- Use `SET LOCAL ROLE authenticated` + `SET LOCAL "request.jwt.claim.sub"` for role testing
- Apply migration to local docker container via `docker exec` when `supabase db test` doesn't automatically pick up new files

## Discoveries
- pgTAP's `is_null()` function has type resolution issues with scalar subqueries returning `TIMESTAMPTZ` — use `ok(expr IS NULL, ...)` instead
- The `# No tests run!` error on `finish()` is a pre-existing pgTAP quirk in Supabase CLI (also present in other test files like `copy_job_plan_test.sql:483`) — does NOT indicate real test failure
- `supabase db test` runs tests via Docker container but doesn't auto-apply migrations from new files — need to `docker exec` into the DB container to apply OR restart supabase. The `supabase stop`/`supabase start` cycle resets from backup, so the migration must be applied separately.
- The `trg_check_pm_schedule_plan_active` trigger requires `job_plans.version_status = 'ACTIVE'` when inserting into `pm_schedules` — test data must set this.

## Accomplished
- ✅ Created `supabase/migrations/20260605000001_pm_schedule_copy.sql` with `copy_pm_schedules_to_asset()` and `copy_pm_schedules_to_plan()`, both SECURITY DEFINER with role check, entity validation, GRANT EXECUTE TO authenticated, and COMMENTS
- ✅ Created `supabase/tests/database/pm_schedule_copy_test.sql` with 13 assertions across 10 test scenarios covering: happy path (count), history reset, frequency calculation, override frequency, cross-plan copy, child exclusion, repeat-call dedup, role rejection, source preservation, and empty source
- ✅ All 13 pgTAP tests pass
- ✅ Updated `tasks.md` with all tasks marked [x]

## Next Steps
- Ready for verify phase

- `supabase/tests/database/pm_schedule_copy_test.sql` — pgTAP test suite (13 assertions, all pass)

observations.title: sdd/job-plan-classification/proposal
observations.content:
# Proposal: Job Plan Classification

## Intent

Planners can't browse job plans by taxonomy — "Show all OVERHAUL plans for centrifugal pumps, filter by criticality A." GEMA has `intervention_type` and `asset_type_id` but no hierarchical tag system. This adds a multi-dimensional classification layer so planners can filter, group, and discover plans by category.

## Scope

### In Scope
- `job_plan_categories` table (self-referencing hierarchy, code unique)
- `job_plan_category_members` M:N bridge table
- 11 seed categories (criticality, frequency, safety, condition, regulatory)
- `v_job_plan_classified` view (aggregated category names + codes)
- `ALTER job_plans` add `work_center`, `frequency_category` columns
- RLS policies (SELECT for all authenticated, DML for PLANNER/ADMIN only)

### Out of Scope
- RxDB schema / offline sync (categories are server-side reference data)
- Frontend category management UI
- Category-based filtering in PM engine or WO generation
- Import/export of category taxonomy

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities
- `job-plan-classification`: Multi-dimensional classification taxonomy for job plans. Hierarchical categories, M:N membership, enriched view, and frequency/work-center metadata on job plans.

### Modified Capabilities
- None

## Approach

Two tables (categories + bridge), seeded with 11 default codes via `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`. View uses `string_agg` to flatten category names per plan. `ALTER job_plans` adds two nullable columns with `CHECK` constraint on `frequency_category`. RLS mirrors existing pattern: `get_user_role() IN ('PLANNER', 'ADMIN')` for DML.

## Affected Areas

| Area | Impact | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `supabase/migrations/` | New | `20260606000001_job_plan_classification.sql` |
| `supabase/tests/database/` | New | `job_plan_classification_test.sql` |

## Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|------|------------|------------|
| Parent category FK blocks seed order | Med | Insert parent-less categories first OR use deferrable constraints |
| Category code collision with future seeds | Low | `ON CONFLICT (code) DO NOTHING` makes seeds idempotent |

## Rollback

Drop `v_job_plan_classified`, both new tables, and revert `ALTER job_plans` columns — all in a single migration reversal.

## Dependencies

- `job_plans` table (exists since `20260531000001`)
- `asset_types` table (referenced in view)
- `get_user_role()` function (exists since RBAC migration)

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Migration runs clean on current `job_plans` schema
- [ ] All 11 seed categories present after migration
- [ ] Category hierarchy works (parent_category_id FK)
- [ ] View returns correct aggregated categories per plan
- [ ] RLS blocks non-PLANNER/ADMIN from inserting members
- [ ] `work_center` and `frequency_category` columns exist with correct CHECK

observations.title: sdd/job-plan-classification/spec
observations.content:
# Job Plan Classification Specification

## Purpose

Multi-dimensional taxonomy for job plans — hierarchical categories with M:N membership, enriched query view, and plan-level work-center/frequency metadata.

## Requirements

### R1: job_plan_categories table

The system MUST provide a `job_plan_categories` table with UUID PK, `code TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL`, `name TEXT NOT NULL`, `description TEXT`, and `parent_category_id UUID` self-referencing FK for hierarchy.

#### Scenario: Table structure

- GIVEN the migration has been applied
- THEN `job_plan_categories` has columns `id`, `code`, `name`, `description`, `parent_category_id`, `created_at`

#### Scenario: Self-reference works

- GIVEN a parent category with code `CRITICALITY_A`
- WHEN inserting a child category with `parent_category_id` pointing to the parent
- THEN the child references the parent correctly

### R2: job_plan_category_members bridge

The system MUST provide a `job_plan_category_members` table with `job_plan_id UUID FK` and `category_id UUID FK` as composite PK.

#### Scenario: Bridge table structure

- GIVEN the migration has been applied
- THEN `job_plan_category_members` has columns `job_plan_id` and `category_id` as PK

#### Scenario: Member assignment works

- GIVEN a job plan with id `P1` and a category with id `C1`
- WHEN inserting `(P1, C1)` into the bridge table
- THEN the member row exists

### R3: Seed data

The system MUST insert at least 11 default categories: `CRITICALITY_A`, `CRITICALITY_B`, `CRITICALITY_C`, `FREQ_DAILY`, `FREQ_WEEKLY`, `FREQ_MONTHLY`, `FREQ_QUARTERLY`, `FREQ_ANNUAL`, `SAFETY_CRITICAL`, `CONDITION_BASED`, `REGULATORY`. The insert MUST use `ON CONFLICT (code) DO NOTHING` for idempotency.

#### Scenario: All seeds present

- GIVEN the migration has been applied
- THEN `SELECT count(*) FROM job_plan_categories` returns at least 11 rows

### R4: v_job_plan_classified view

The system MUST provide a view `v_job_plan_classified` that joins `job_plans`, `asset_types`, `job_plan_category_members`, and `job_plan_categories`, aggregating category names via `string_agg` and codes via `array_agg`.

#### Scenario: View aggregates correctly

- GIVEN a job plan assigned to categories "Criticality A" and "Safety Critical"
- THEN `v_job_plan_classified` shows that plan with `categories` containing both names and `category_codes` containing both codes

### R5: RLS policies

The system MUST enforce RLS on both tables: `authenticated` users can SELECT; only users with role `PLANNER` or `ADMIN` can INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE.

#### Scenario: SELECT allowed for all authenticated

- GIVEN any authenticated user
- WHEN querying either table
- THEN SELECT succeeds

#### Scenario: INSERT restricted to PLANNER/ADMIN

- GIVEN a non-PLANNER/ADMIN authenticated user
- WHEN inserting into either table
- THEN the insert is blocked

### R6: job_plans ALTER columns

The system MUST `ALTER job_plans ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS work_center TEXT` and `frequency_category TEXT` with a CHECK constraint restricting values to `DAILY`, `WEEKLY`, `MONTHLY`, `QUARTERLY`, `SEMI_ANNUAL`, `ANNUAL`, `CONDITION_BASED`, `ONE_TIME`.

#### Scenario: work_center column exists

- GIVEN the migration has been applied
- THEN `job_plans` has a nullable `work_center` column

#### Scenario: frequency_category CHECK works

- GIVEN a job plan
- WHEN setting `frequency_category` to `'DAILY'`
- THEN the update succeeds
- WHEN setting `frequency_category` to `'INVALID'`
- THEN the update fails with a CHECK violation

### R7: Idempotency

All DDL MUST use `IF NOT EXISTS`. All seed inserts MUST use `ON CONFLICT (code) DO NOTHING`. All ALTER ADD COLUMN MUST use `IF NOT EXISTS`.

#### Scenario: Repeated migration is safe

- GIVEN the migration has already been applied once
- WHEN applying it again
- THEN no errors are raised

## Test Scenarios Summary

| ID | Scenario | Type |
|----|----------|------|
| S1 | Categories table has correct columns | Schema |
| S2 | Self-referencing hierarchy works | Integration |
| S3 | All 11 seed categories inserted | Data |
| S4 | Member bridge assigns plan to category | Integration |
| S5 | View aggregates categories via string_agg | Query |
| S6 | work_center and frequency_category columns exist | Schema |
| S7 | RLS blocks non-PLANNER/ADMIN from inserting | Security |

observations.title: sdd/bi-views-analytics/proposal
observations.content:
# Proposal: BI Views & Analytics Layer

## Intent

Planners can't answer PM completion rates, cost per plan, or resource demand. GEMA has `pm_due_calendar` but no analytics layer. This adds star-schema views for BI tooling.

## Scope

### In Scope
- `v_dim_job_plan`, `v_dim_asset` — dimension views
- `v_fact_wo_execution` — PM WO fact (time, cost, hours variance)
- `mv_pm_compliance_monthly` — compliance by intervention_type
- `mv_plan_cost_history` — cost by plan + month
- `v_resource_demand`, `v_backlog_summary` — resource views
- GRANT SELECT + COMMENT ON all views
- pgTAP test suite

### Out of Scope
- MV auto-refresh schedule (manual / pg_cron in Phase 0)
- BI dashboard templates (.twbx/.pbix)
- Separate `analytics` schema (uses public per GEMA convention)
- Historical backfill
- RxDB schema changes

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities
- `bi-views-analytics`: Star-schema analytics layer — dimensions, facts, MVs for compliance/cost, resource demand, and backlog. Read-only via SELECT grants.

### Modified Capabilities
- None

## Approach

Single migration: 7 views in `public` with `v_`/`mv_` prefixes. Dimensions wrap base tables. Fact view computes `EXTRACT(EPOCH ...)` time metrics and hours variance from `labor_records`. MVs aggregate monthly via `DATE_TRUNC`. Resource views project 12 weeks from `pm_schedules` + `job_plan_labor`.

## Affected Areas

| Area | Impact | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `supabase/migrations/` | New | Migration + grants + comments |
| `supabase/tests/database/` | New | pgTAP test suite |

## Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|------|------------|------------|
| MV refresh on production | Low | Low-traffic window / on-demand |
| Fact view perf on large WO | Med | Existing indexes on wo_type, completed_at |
| RLS exposes cost data | Low | Views inherit RLS from base tables |

## Rollback

`DROP VIEW` all 7, `DROP MATERIALIZED VIEW` both MVs. Grants auto-revoke. Single reversal.

## Dependencies

- `work_orders`, `job_plans`, `assets`, `asset_types`, `pm_schedules` (exist)
- `job_plan_labor`, `work_order_labor_estimates` (since `20260531000001`)
- `labor_records` (since `20260526000002`)
- `generate_due_preventive_work_orders()` (since `20260531000002`)

## Success Criteria

- [ ] All 7 views return correct columns with seed data
- [ ] `v_fact_wo_execution` computes hours variance correctly
- [ ] MVs refresh with `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY`
- [ ] `authenticated` role can SELECT all views
- [ ] All `COMMENT ON` descriptions in `information_schema`

observations.title: sdd/bi-views-analytics/spec
observations.content:
# BI Views & Analytics Specification

## Purpose

Star-schema analytics layer with dimension views, fact views, materialized views, and resource projections — all read-only, exposed via `public` schema with `v_` / `mv_` prefixes, accessible to `authenticated` role.

## Requirements

### R1: v_dim_job_plan dimension view

The system MUST provide a `v_dim_job_plan` view exposing `job_plan_id`, `code`, `description`, `intervention_type`, `estimated_hours`, `asset_type_name`, `is_active`, `version`, and `created_at`.

#### Scenario: Dimension view returns correct columns

- GIVEN the migration has been applied
- THEN `v_dim_job_plan` contains columns `job_plan_id`, `code`, `description`, `intervention_type`, `estimated_hours`, `asset_type_name`, `is_active`, `version`, `created_at`

### R2: v_dim_asset dimension view

The system MUST provide a `v_dim_asset` view exposing asset identity columns: `id`, `equipment_id`, `description`, `asset_type_id`, `criticality`, `location`, `site`.

#### Scenario: Asset dimension view columns

- GIVEN the migration has been applied
- THEN `v_dim_asset` contains columns `id`, `equipment_id`, `description`, `asset_type_id`, `criticality`, `location`, `site`

### R3: v_fact_wo_execution fact view

The system MUST provide a `v_fact_wo_execution` view with one row per PM-generated WO, including `wo_id`, `job_plan_id`, `asset_id`, `reported_date`, `completed_date`, `intervention_type`, `hours_from_report_to_complete`, `total_estimated_cost`, `estimated_hours`, `estimated_parts_cost`, `estimated_labor_cost`, and `hours_variance`.

The `hours_variance` column MUST compute `estimated_hours - SUM(labor_records.hours_worked)` for completed WOs, NULL otherwise.

#### Scenario: Fact view aggregates time metrics

- GIVEN a PM WO with `reported_at = '2026-01-01 08:00'` and `completed_at = '2026-01-01 12:00'`
- THEN `hours_from_report_to_complete` equals 4.0

#### Scenario: Fact view computes hours variance

- GIVEN a completed PM WO with `estimated_hours = 8` and `labor_records` summing to 6.5 hours
- THEN `hours_variance` equals 1.5

#### Scenario: Fact view filters to PM only

- GIVEN a WO with `wo_type = 'CM'` (corrective)
- THEN it is NOT included in `v_fact_wo_execution`

### R4: mv_pm_compliance_monthly materialized view

The system MUST provide a `mv_pm_compliance_monthly` materialized view aggregating compliance rate by `month` and `intervention_type`, with columns `month`, `intervention_type`, `scheduled_count`, `completed_count`, and `compliance_rate` as percentage.

#### Scenario: Materialized view can be refreshed

- GIVEN the MV has been created
- WHEN executing `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY mv_pm_compliance_monthly`
- THEN it succeeds without error

#### Scenario: Compliance rate is correct

- GIVEN 10 PM schedules due in a month, 7 completed
- THEN `compliance_rate` equals 70.0

### R5: mv_plan_cost_history materialized view

The system MUST provide a `mv_plan_cost_history` materialized view aggregating cost by `job_plan_id`, `job_plan_code`, `intervention_type`, `execution_month`, with columns `execution_count`, `avg_total_cost`, and `total_cost`.

#### Scenario: Cost aggregation works

- GIVEN a plan with 3 completed WOs in the same month, each costing 100
- THEN `execution_count` = 3, `avg_total_cost` = 100, `total_cost` = 300

### R6: v_resource_demand view

The system MUST provide a `v_resource_demand` view projecting labor demand by `week_start`, `trade`, `planned_hours`, `schedule_count`, and `required_fte` for the next 12 weeks from `CURRENT_DATE`.

#### Scenario: Resource demand projects future labor

- GIVEN a `pm_schedule` with `next_target_date` within 12 weeks, linked to a plan with 2 MECHANIC entries of 4 hours each
- THEN `v_resource_demand` includes a row with `trade = 'MECHANIC'`, `planned_hours >= 8`

### R7: v_backlog_summary view

The system MUST provide a `v_backlog_summary` view aggregating open WO backlog by `trade` with `open_wo_count` and `backlog_hours` (sum of `estimated_hours * head_count` from `work_order_labor_estimates`).

#### Scenario: Backlog aggregates open WOs

- GIVEN 3 open WOs in WAPPR/APPROVED/INPRG with MECHANIC labor totaling 16 hours
- THEN `v_backlog_summary` includes a row with `trade = 'MECHANIC'`, `open_wo_count >= 1`

### R8: GRANT SELECT to authenticated role

The system MUST `GRANT SELECT ON ALL VIEWS IN SCHEMA public TO authenticated` so the `authenticated` role can query all analytics views through Supabase REST API.

#### Scenario: Authenticated role can query views

- GIVEN any authenticated user session
- THEN `SELECT * FROM v_dim_job_plan` returns data without permission error

## Test Scenarios Summary

| ID | Scenario | Type |
|----|----------|------|
| S1 | Dimension views return correct columns | Schema |
| S2 | Fact view aggregates time and cost correctly | Query |
| S3 | Materialized views can be refreshed | Admin |
| S4 | Resource views project demand correctly | Query |

observations.title: sdd/bi-views-analytics/design
observations.content:
# Design: BI Views & Analytics Layer

## Technical Approach

Single migration: 7 views in `public` with `v_`/`mv_` prefixes. Dimensions wrap base tables; fact view computes time/cost via `EXTRACT(EPOCH ...)` + `labor_records`. MVs use `DATE_TRUNC` for monthly bucketing. All views are `STABLE` (not `SECURITY DEFINER`) — RLS on base tables filters automatically. Map: R1→v_dim_job_plan, R2→v_dim_asset, R3→v_fact_wo_execution, R4→mv_pm_compliance_monthly, R5→mv_plan_cost_history, R6→v_resource_demand, R7→v_backlog_summary, R8→GRANT SELECT.

## Architecture Decisions

| # | Decision | Options | Tradeoffs | Chosen |
|---|----------|---------|-----------|--------|
| D1 | Schema placement | (a) `public` with `v_` prefix (b) separate `analytics` schema | (b) cleaner isolation but breaks GEMA convention — all existing views are in `public`. (a) consistent, no query path changes | **public schema** — follows existing `pm_due_calendar` pattern |
| D2 | MV refresh strategy | (a) on-demand manual (b) pg_cron auto (c) trigger-based | (b)/(c) add infra complexity for Phase 0 data that changes daily. (a) simple, planner clicks "Refresh" in BI tool | **On-demand** — `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY` via SQL or pg_cron later |
| D3 | Security model | (a) `SECURITY DEFINER` (b) `STABLE` default | (a) bypasses RLS — wrong for analytics that should respect asset visibility. (b) inherits underlying RLS automatically | **STABLE (default)** — RLS on base tables filters what the view returns |
| D4 | Hours variance calculation | (a) `estimated_hours - SUM(labor_records)` (b) `estimated_hours - work_orders.actual_hours` | (b) uses pre-calculated field from `trg_labor_sum_hours` trigger, simpler. (a) more accurate — computes at query time from raw records | **`estimated_hours - SUM(labor_records.hours_worked)`** — direct from source, no dependency on trigger timing |

## Data Flow

```
job_plans ─────────────► v_dim_job_plan ──┐
assets ───────────────► v_dim_asset        ├──► Supabase REST (SELECT)
work_orders + labor    ─► v_fact_wo_exec   │    Direct PG (Power BI)
pm_schedules           ─► mv_pm_compliance │
work_orders (COMP)     ─► mv_plan_cost     ┘
pm_sched + labor       ─► v_resource_demand
work_orders (open)     ─► v_backlog_summary
```

## File Changes

| File | Action | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `supabase/migrations/20260608000001_bi_views_analytics.sql` | Create | All 7 views, materialized views, grants, comments |
| `supabase/tests/database/bi_views_analytics_test.sql` | Create | pgTAP: schema, query correctness, refresh, grants |

### Migration Structure

| Section | Content |
|---------|---------|
| 1 — Dimension Views | `v_dim_job_plan`, `v_dim_asset` |
| 2 — Fact View | `v_fact_wo_execution` with time/cost/variance |
| 3 — Materialized Views | `mv_pm_compliance_monthly`, `mv_plan_cost_history` |
| 4 — Resource Views | `v_resource_demand`, `v_backlog_summary` |
| 5 — Grants | `GRANT SELECT ON ALL VIEWS IN SCHEMA public TO authenticated` |
| 6 — Comments | `COMMENT ON VIEW/COLUMN` for all 7 views |

## Testing Strategy

| Layer | What to Test | Approach |
|-------|-------------|----------|
| Schema | All 7 views exist with expected columns | pgTAP `has_view`, `columns_are` |
| Fact view | Time metric calculation, hours variance, PM filter | Insert test WO + labor_records, verify output |
| Materialized views | Refresh succeeds, compliance/cost aggregation | `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW`, verify row counts |
| Resource views | Demand projection within 12-week window, backlog hours | Insert test schedules/labor, verify aggregation |
| Grants | `authenticated` can SELECT, views are accessible | `set_role('authenticated')` + simple SELECT |
| Idempotency | Re-running migration raises no errors | `BEGIN; apply; apply; ROLLBACK;` |

## Migration / Rollout

Purely additive — no data migration, no table changes. Views compute from existing data. Rollback: `DROP VIEW` all 7 views + `DROP MATERIALIZED VIEW` both MVs. Grant revocation is automatic on DROP.

## Open Questions

- [ ] Should `mv_pm_compliance_monthly` use `CONCURRENTLY` for refresh? Yes — avoids table locks, requires unique index on MV.

observations.title: sdd/safety-gate-enforcement/proposal
observations.content:
# Proposal: Safety Gate Enforcement

## Intent

`work_order_safety_requirements` are snapshotted at WO generation but are purely informational — they tell the technician what's needed but don't BLOCK starting the WO. This change wires them to the WO lifecycle: APPROVED→INPRG is blocked until mandatory safety requirements are fulfilled, and permit activation auto-satisfies linked requirements.

## Scope

### In Scope
- Schema: `work_permit_id`, `fulfillment_status`, `waived_by`, `waiver_reason` on `work_order_safety_requirements`
- Trigger `trg_check_safety_gate()` — BEFORE UPDATE on work_orders, blocks APPROVED→INPRG if mandatory safety pending
- Trigger `trg_safety_permit_fulfilled()` — AFTER UPDATE on work_permits, auto-updates fulfillment_status when permit→ACTIVE
- ADMIN role bypasses the gate
- pgTAP tests (6 scenarios)

### Out of Scope
- Frontend UI for waivers, permit linking, or gate error display
- RxDB schema changes
- LOTO-specific gate enforcement

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities
- `safety-gate-enforcement`: mandatory safety gate that blocks WO start until all permits are active or waived, with ADMIN bypass and auto-fulfillment on permit activation

### Modified Capabilities
None

## Approach

Two database triggers. BEFORE UPDATE on work_orders checks lifecycle_phase transition APPROVED→INPRG and validates no mandatory fulfillment_status = 'PENDING'. ADMIN bypass via get_user_role(). AFTER UPDATE on work_permits detects ACTIVE status and sets matching work_order_safety_requirements.fulfillment_status = 'FULFILLED'.

## Affected Areas
| Area | Impact | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `supabase/migrations/20260608000001_safety_gate_enforcement.sql` | New | ALTER + 2 triggers + RLS |
| `supabase/tests/database/safety_gate_test.sql` | New | 6 pgTAP scenarios |

## Risks
| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|------|------------|------------|
| Existing WOs with pending safety can't start | Low | ADMIN bypass; WOs already INPRG won't re-fire |
| Gate blocks legitimate WOs if permit linking incomplete | Low | Non-mandatory don't block; waiver path exists |

## Rollback Plan

DROP triggers, DROP functions, ALTER TABLE DROP COLUMN for the 4 new columns. No data loss.

## Dependencies
- safety-permits migration (work_permits table + FSM)
- job-plan-structured migration (work_order_safety_requirements table)

## Success Criteria
- [ ] Gate blocks INPRG when mandatory safety is PENDING
- [ ] Gate allows INPRG when all mandatory safety is FULFILLED
- [ ] Non-mandatory requirements don't block the gate
- [ ] ADMIN can bypass the gate
- [ ] Permit ACTIVE triggers auto-fulfillment
- [ ] All 4 new columns exist and are constrained

observations.title: sdd/safety-gate-enforcement/spec
observations.content:
# Safety Gate Enforcement — Specification

## Purpose

Define the enforcement layer that links work order safety requirements to permit lifecycle. When a WO transitions APPROVED→INPRG, all mandatory safety requirements MUST be fulfilled or waived. Permit activation auto-satisfies linked requirements.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Schema Extension

The system MUST add 4 columns to work_order_safety_requirements: work_permit_id (UUID FK→work_permits(id), nullable), fulfillment_status (TEXT DEFAULT 'PENDING' CHECK IN 'PENDING','IN_PROGRESS','FULFILLED','WAIVED'), waived_by (UUID FK→user_profiles(id)), waiver_reason (TEXT). Existing is_fulfilled boolean SHALL remain unchanged.

#### Scenario: Migration creates all 4 columns
- GIVEN migration has been applied
- WHEN querying work_order_safety_requirements schema
- THEN all 4 columns SHALL exist with correct types and constraints

### Requirement: Status Gate (Hard Block)

BEFORE UPDATE trigger trg_check_safety_gate on work_orders. Fires when lifecycle_phase transitions APPROVED→INPRG. Raises exception if any mandatory requirement has fulfillment_status = 'PENDING'. Bypasses when get_user_role() = 'ADMIN'.

#### Scenario: Gate blocks INPRG when mandatory PENDING
- GIVEN a WO with lifecycle_phase APPROVED and a mandatory safety requirement PENDING
- WHEN a non-ADMIN sets lifecycle_phase to INPRG
- THEN the trigger SHALL raise an exception

#### Scenario: Gate allows INPRG when all mandatory fulfilled
- GIVEN a WO with lifecycle_phase APPROVED and all mandatory fulfilled or waived
- WHEN a user sets lifecycle_phase to INPRG
- THEN the update SHALL succeed

#### Scenario: Non-mandatory don't block
- GIVEN a WO with a non-mandatory requirement PENDING and no mandatory PENDING
- WHEN a user sets lifecycle_phase to INPRG
- THEN the update SHALL succeed

#### Scenario: ADMIN bypass
- GIVEN a WO with mandatory safety PENDING
- WHEN an ADMIN user sets lifecycle_phase to INPRG
- THEN the update SHALL succeed

#### Scenario: Non-gate transitions pass through
- GIVEN any safety fulfillment state
- WHEN a user sets lifecycle_phase to any transition other than APPROVED→INPRG
- THEN the update SHALL succeed

### Requirement: Auto-fulfillment on Permit Activation

AFTER UPDATE trigger trg_safety_permit_fulfilled on work_permits. When permit_status transitions to ACTIVE, updates work_order_safety_requirements.fulfillment_status = 'FULFILLED' for matching work_permit_id.

#### Scenario: Permit activation fulfills requirement
- GIVEN a safety requirement linked to permit P via work_permit_id
- WHEN permit P transitions to ACTIVE
- THEN fulfillment_status for that row SHALL become 'FULFILLED'

### Requirement: Waiver

SAFETY_OFFICER and ADMIN roles MAY set fulfillment_status = 'WAIVED' with non-null waiver_reason and waived_by.

#### Scenario: SAFETY_OFFICER waives a requirement
- GIVEN a mandatory requirement PENDING
- WHEN SAFETY_OFFICER sets fulfillment_status=WAIVED with reason
- THEN the update SHALL succeed and gate SHALL allow INPRG

observations.title: sdd/safety-gate-enforcement/design
observations.content:
# Design: Safety Gate Enforcement

## Technical Approach

Two BEFORE/AFTER UPDATE triggers enforce the safety-permit linkage at the database level. Migration alters work_order_safety_requirements adding permit linking columns, then installs both triggers. Gate trigger fires only on APPROVED→INPRG transitions. Auto-fulfill trigger fires on permit→ACTIVE. ADMIN bypass via get_user_role() check.

## Architecture Decisions

| # | Decision | Choice | Alternative | Rationale |
|---|----------|--------|-------------|-----------|
| D1 | Trigger timing | BEFORE UPDATE on work_orders | App-layer check | DB-level enforcement consistent with competency gate and permit FSM triggers |
| D2 | Mandatory only | Only is_mandatory=true blocks | All requirements | Non-mandatory are advisory; matches Maximo Safety Plans behavior |
| D3 | ADMIN bypass | Gate skips check for ADMIN | No bypass | Unblock operational emergencies; audit via existing audit_logs |
| D4 | Permit trigger timing | AFTER UPDATE on work_permits | BEFORE | Permit FSM must validate first; fulfillment is a side effect, not a precondition |

## Data Flow

Safe: PM gen → requirements created (PENDING) → permit linked → permit→ACTIVE → fulfillment='FULFILLED' → APPROVED→INPRG → gate passes. Blocked: mandatory PENDING → APPROVED→INPRG → EXCEPTION. Bypass: ADMIN skips check.

## File Changes
| File | Action | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `supabase/migrations/20260608000001_safety_gate_enforcement.sql` | Create | ALTER + 2 triggers + COMMENTS |
| `supabase/tests/database/safety_gate_test.sql` | Create | 6 pgTAP scenarios |

## Migration Structure

SECTION 1: ALTER work_order_safety_requirements ADD COLUMNS (work_permit_id, fulfillment_status, waived_by, waiver_reason). SECTION 2: CREATE fn_check_safety_gate() — checks lifecycle_phase transition, SELECT for PENDING mandatory, RAISE if found AND role != ADMIN. SECTION 3: CREATE TRIGGER trg_check_safety_gate BEFORE UPDATE ON work_orders. SECTION 4: CREATE fn_safety_permit_fulfilled() — WHEN permit_status='ACTIVE' AND OLD.permit_status!='ACTIVE', UPDATE fulfillment_status='FULFILLED' WHERE work_permit_id=NEW.id. SECTION 5: CREATE TRIGGER trg_safety_permit_fulfilled AFTER UPDATE ON work_permits. SECTION 6: COMMENTS (Spanish, project convention).

## Testing Strategy
| Layer | Approach |
|-------|----------|
| Schema | pgTAP has_column() for all 4 new columns |
| Gate | Direct UPDATE lifecycle, expect exception or success based on fulfillment |
| Bypass | Execute as ADMIN role, expect success despite PENDING |
| Auto-fulfill | Set permit ACTIVE, verify requirement status |
| Non-mandatory | Non-mandatory PENDING, expect gate pass |

## Rollout
Standard Supabase migration. No data backfill needed. Existing is_fulfilled boolean retained for backward compat.

## Goal
Ejecutar 5 SDD FF completos (automático, híbrido) para features Phase 0 de Job Plans Module: Scheduling Fix, PM Schedule Copy, Job Plan Classification, BI Views, Safety Gate Enforcement.

## Instructions
- Modo automático para SDD (correr fases sin pausar)
- Store híbrido (openspec + engram) para toda la documentación
- Las features 5.2 (WO Snapshot) y 5.5 (Scheduling Fix) se combinaron en un solo cambio porque ambas modificaban generate_due_preventive_work_orders()
- Tablas work_order_task_snapshots y work_order_material_snapshots ya existían desde migración job-plans-foundation — el snapshot pattern ya estaba implementado

## Discoveries
- **WO Snapshot ya existía**: Las tablas snapshot y su población en el PM engine ya estaban implementadas desde job-plans-foundation. Batch A se re-escaló a solo scheduling fixes.
- **Floating schedule bug**: El engine usaba CURRENT_DATE en vez de last_completion_date para avanzar schedules flotantes. Corregido.
- **Backfill postergado**: Las WOs anteriores a la creación de snapshot tables no tienen datos — queda como deuda técnica para otro cambio.
- **GRANT SELECT ON ALL VIEWS IN SCHEMA**: PostgreSQL NO soporta esta sintaxis. Hubo que hacer GRANT por vista individual.
- **PostgreSQL UPDATE semantics**: En un UPDATE, las expresiones del SET leen valores OLD de las columnas, no los nuevos. Afecta el cálculo de next_target_date cuando last_completion_date se setea en el mismo UPDATE — pero el comportamiento es correcto porque la intención es avanzar desde la completion anterior.
- **Safety gate + permit trigger**: El trigger de auto-fulfillment en work_permits usa la columna permit_status (no status como estaba en el spec original). Corregido en implementación.
- **get_user_role() mock en tests**: Para testear ADMIN bypass del safety gate, hubo que mockear get_user_role() dentro de savepoints porque SET LOCAL no es accesible desde auth.uid() dentro de triggers SECURITY DEFINER.

## Accomplished
- ✅ **Batch A: Scheduling Fix (wo-snapshot-scheduling-fix)** — 14/14 tests. lead_days + grace_period_days en pm_schedules y work_orders. Floating corregido (avanza desde last_completion_date). WO se genera lead_days antes del due date.

- ✅ **Batch E: Safety Gate Enforcement (safety-gate-enforcement)** — 13/13 tests. Gate trigger bloquea APPROVED→INPRG si safety mandatory está PENDING. Permit auto-fulfill trigger. ADMIN bypass.

## Next Steps
- Backfill de snapshot tables para WOs anteriores a job-plans-foundation (deuda técnica documentada)

observations.title: sdd/meter-based-pm-trigger/proposal
observations.content:
# Proposal: Meter-Based PM Trigger

## Intent

Enable PM schedules to trigger work orders based on meter readings (usage-based/condition-based maintenance). Currently `generate_due_preventive_work_orders()` only evaluates calendar-based schedules (`time_frequency_days`). Schedules configured with `meter_frequency_value` are stored but never processed. This change adds the event-driven pipeline: meter reading INSERT → trigger → function → WO creation for all matching meter-based schedules.

## Scope

### In Scope

- Migration: ALTER `pm_schedules` with `meter_id`, `meter_trigger_value`, `meter_reset_on_completion`
- Function: `generate_meter_pm_work_orders(p_meter_id UUID, p_reading_value NUMERIC)`
- Trigger: `trg_meter_reading_pm_trigger` on `meter_readings` AFTER INSERT
- Dedup guard: prevent duplicate WOs for the same schedule within the same meter window
- pgTAP tests for function and trigger behavior

### Out of Scope

- Edge Function wrapper (pure SQL trigger sufficient for Phase 1)
- RxDB schema updates (no application-layer changes)
- Calendar-based PM engine changes (existing function unchanged)
- Seasonal/event-based PM triggers (future phases)
- Frontend UI for configuring meter-based schedules

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

- `meter-based-pm-trigger-schema`: `pm_schedules` gains `meter_id`, `meter_trigger_value`, `meter_reset_on_completion`
- `meter-based-pm-generation`: `generate_meter_pm_work_orders()` creates WOs when a meter reading crosses a schedule's threshold
- `meter-reading-trigger`: `trg_meter_reading_pm_trigger` hooks into `meter_readings` INSERT

### Modified Capabilities

None — additive only. The existing `generate_due_preventive_work_orders()` is not touched.

## Approach

Single idempotent migration with three sections:

| Section | What | Why Separate |
|---------|------|--------------|
| Schema | ALTER `pm_schedules` ADD COLUMN | Columns must exist before function references them |
| Function | `generate_meter_pm_work_orders()` | Core logic: find schedules, check thresholds, create WOs, dedup |
| Trigger | `trg_meter_reading_pm_trigger` | Event-driven entry point; calls function per reading |

The function is **separate** from `generate_due_preventive_work_orders()` because meter-based PM is event-driven (trigger on INSERT), while calendar-based is scheduled (pg_cron). Merging them would create a function that works both as a trigger and a scheduled job — that's a design smell.

**Dedup strategy**: Before creating a WO, query `work_orders` for an existing WO with the same `job_plan_id` and `asset_id` where `reported_at >= schedule.last_completion_date` (or the meter's last reading at trigger time). If found, skip.

**Meter frequency window**: If `meter_frequency_value` is set, the function checks `p_reading_value >= previous_trigger_reading + meter_frequency_value` to avoid re-triggering on every reading within the same window.

## Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|------|------------|------------|
| Trigger performance on high-frequency meter readings | Low | Function is lightweight (indexed queries); meter readings are not high-frequency in CMMS context |
| Trigger creates duplicate WOs for same schedule | Low | Dedup check before INSERT; see approach |
| Meter reset on completion cycles incorrectly | Low | `meter_reset_on_completion` is a boolean that tracks state; the function only advances when TRUE and reading exceeds the last trigger value |

## Rollback Plan

1. `DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_meter_reading_pm_trigger ON meter_readings`
2. `DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS generate_meter_pm_work_orders`
3. `ALTER TABLE pm_schedules DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS meter_id, DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS meter_trigger_value, DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS meter_reset_on_completion`

No data loss on rollback — columns are additive and nullable.

## Dependencies

- `pm_schedules` table (exists)
- `meters` table (exists)
- `meter_readings` table (exists)
- `work_orders` table (exists)
- `get_user_role()` helper for RLS consistency

## Success Criteria

- [ ] `pm_schedules` gains `meter_id`, `meter_trigger_value`, `meter_reset_on_completion` with correct FK and defaults
- [ ] `generate_meter_pm_work_orders()` creates WOs only when reading >= meter_trigger_value
- [ ] Dedup: same schedule does NOT generate duplicate WOs within same meter window
- [ ] Trigger calls the function on every `meter_readings` INSERT
- [ ] Function is SECURITY DEFINER, trigger runs as owner
- [ ] Migration idempotent — safe to run repeatedly
- [ ] pgTAP tests cover: basic trigger, frequency window, dedup, meter_reset, no match, multiple schedules

observations.title: sdd/meter-based-pm-trigger/spec
observations.content:
# Meter-Based PM Trigger Specification

## Purpose

Extend `pm_schedules` with meter-trigger columns and create the event-driven pipeline that generates work orders when a meter reading crosses a schedule's configured threshold. This enables usage-based preventive maintenance (e.g., "Every 500 hours") independent of the calendar-based PM engine.

## Requirements

### Requirement: meter_id on pm_schedules

The system MUST add a `meter_id` column to `pm_schedules` that references which meter to watch:

| Column | Type | Constraints |
|--------|------|-------------|
| meter_id | UUID | nullable, FK → meters(id) |

#### Scenario: pm_schedules gains meter_id

- GIVEN a schedule with `time_frequency_days` = NULL
- WHEN the schedule is configured with a valid `meter_id`
- THEN the schedule SHALL be eligible for meter-based triggering

#### Scenario: meter_id references existing meter

- GIVEN a meter with id = 'abc-123' exists
- WHEN a pm_schedule is created with meter_id = 'abc-123'
- THEN the FK constraint SHALL be satisfied

#### Scenario: Invalid meter_id rejected

- GIVEN a meter with id = 'abc-123' does NOT exist
- WHEN a pm_schedule is created with meter_id = 'nonexistent-uuid'
- THEN the INSERT MUST fail with foreign key violation

### Requirement: meter_trigger_value on pm_schedules

The system MUST add a `meter_trigger_value NUMERIC` column to `pm_schedules`:

| Column | Type | Constraints |
|--------|------|-------------|
| meter_trigger_value | NUMERIC | nullable |

`meter_trigger_value` defines the reading value at which the schedule triggers. A schedule SHALL be considered meter-based ONLY when both `meter_id` and `meter_trigger_value` are NOT NULL.

#### Scenario: Meter-triggered schedule definition

- GIVEN a schedule with meter_id = 'abc-123' and meter_trigger_value = 500
- WHEN a meter reading with value >= 500 is inserted for meter 'abc-123'
- THEN the schedule SHALL be eligible to generate a WO

#### Scenario: NULL meter_trigger_value means no meter trigger

- GIVEN a schedule with meter_id = 'abc-123' and meter_trigger_value = NULL
- WHEN evaluating the schedule
- THEN the schedule SHALL NOT be considered meter-based regardless of meter_id being set

### Requirement: meter_reset_on_completion on pm_schedules

The system MUST add a `meter_reset_on_completion BOOLEAN` column to `pm_schedules`:

| Column | Type | Default | Constraints |
|--------|------|---------|-------------|
| meter_reset_on_completion | BOOLEAN | false | NOT NULL |

When `meter_reset_on_completion = true`, the schedule SHALL track the last trigger reading and only re-trigger when the next reading exceeds `last_trigger_reading + meter_trigger_value` (or `meter_frequency_value`). When `false`, the schedule SHALL trigger every time a reading meets or exceeds the threshold, subject to the dedup guard.

#### Scenario: meter_reset enabled — re-triggers at next window

- GIVEN a schedule with meter_trigger_value = 500, meter_reset_on_completion = true
- GIVEN the last trigger reading was at value 500
- WHEN a new reading of 750 is inserted
- THEN a WO SHALL be generated (750 >= 500, and 750 >= 500 + 0 since no meter_frequency_value)
- WHEN a new reading of 900 is inserted
- THEN the dedup guard SHALL prevent a duplicate WO unless meter_frequency_value defines a window

#### Scenario: meter_reset disabled — dedup still applies

- GIVEN a schedule with meter_trigger_value = 500, meter_reset_on_completion = false
- WHEN a reading of 500 is inserted and a WO is created
- WHEN another reading of 500 is inserted
- THEN the dedup guard SHALL prevent a duplicate WO (same meter window, same schedule)

### Requirement: generate_meter_pm_work_orders() Function

The system MUST create a function `generate_meter_pm_work_orders(p_meter_id UUID, p_reading_value NUMERIC)` that:

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Returns | INT (number of WOs created) |
| Language | plpgsql |
| Security | SECURITY DEFINER |
| Search Path | SET search_path = public |

The function SHALL:

1. Query ALL `pm_schedules` where:
   - `meter_id = p_meter_id`
   - `meter_trigger_value IS NOT NULL`
   - `p_reading_value >= meter_trigger_value`

2. For each matching schedule, check the frequency window:
   - If `meter_frequency_value` is set: `p_reading_value >= last_trigger_reading + meter_frequency_value`
   - Where `last_trigger_reading` is the MAX reading value from `meter_readings` at the time of the last WO generation for this schedule

3. For schedules that pass the frequency check, create a WO:
   - `wo_type = 'PM'`
   - `lifecycle_phase = 'WAPPR'`
   - `job_plan_id` from the schedule
   - `asset_id` from the schedule
   - `symptom_note` describing the meter trigger context

4. Update the schedule:
   - `last_completion_date = NOW()`
   - Optionally track the trigger reading for window calculation

5. Return the count of WOs created

#### Scenario: Function creates WO on meter threshold

- GIVEN a schedule with meter_id = 'M1', meter_trigger_value = 500, job_plan_id = 'JP1', asset_id = 'A1'
- WHEN `generate_meter_pm_work_orders('M1', 500)` is called
- THEN a WO SHALL be created with job_plan_id = 'JP1', asset_id = 'A1', wo_type = 'PM'
- AND the function SHALL return 1

#### Scenario: Function ignores sub-threshold readings

- GIVEN a schedule with meter_trigger_value = 500
- WHEN `generate_meter_pm_work_orders('M1', 300)` is called
- THEN the function SHALL return 0
- AND no WO SHALL be created

#### Scenario: Function handles multiple schedules on same meter

- GIVEN two schedules with meter_id = 'M1': one with meter_trigger_value = 500, another with meter_trigger_value = 1000
- WHEN `generate_meter_pm_work_orders('M1', 1000)` is called
- THEN a WO SHALL be created for BOTH schedules (1000 >= 500 AND 1000 >= 1000)
- AND the function SHALL return 2

### Requirement: Dedup Guard

The function MUST prevent creating duplicate WOs for the same schedule within the same meter trigger window.

**Dedup logic**: Before creating a WO for a schedule, check if a WO already exists in `work_orders` where:
- `job_plan_id` matches the schedule's `job_plan_id`
- `asset_id` matches the schedule's `asset_id`
- `reported_at >= schedule.last_completion_date` (if last_completion_date is not NULL)

If such a WO exists, skip WO creation for that schedule.

#### Scenario: Dedup prevents duplicate WO

- GIVEN a schedule that just generated a WO at reading 500
- WHEN `generate_meter_pm_work_orders('M1', 500)` is called again (same reading, re-triggered)
- THEN the function SHALL return 0
- AND no duplicate WO SHALL be created

#### Scenario: Dedup allows new WO after completion

- GIVEN a schedule that generated a WO at reading 500, and that WO has been completed
- GIVEN `last_completion_date` was updated
- WHEN `generate_meter_pm_work_orders('M1', 1000)` is called
- AND 1000 >= 500 (meter_trigger_value)
- AND the dedup check finds no open WO after last_completion_date for this window
- THEN a new WO SHALL be created

### Requirement: Trigger on meter_readings AFTER INSERT

The system MUST create a trigger `trg_meter_reading_pm_trigger` on `meter_readings`:

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Timing | AFTER INSERT |
| For Each | ROW |
| Function | `generate_meter_pm_work_orders(NEW.meter_id, NEW.reading_value)` |
| Security | Runs as owner (trigger owner) |

#### Scenario: Trigger fires on INSERT

- GIVEN a meter reading with meter_id = 'M1' and reading_value = 500
- WHEN a row is inserted into `meter_readings`
- THEN the trigger SHALL fire
- AND `generate_meter_pm_work_orders('M1', 500)` SHALL be executed

#### Scenario: Trigger does not fire on UPDATE

- GIVEN an existing meter reading row
- WHEN the row is UPDATED
- THEN the trigger SHALL NOT fire (AFTER INSERT only)

### Requirement: SECURITY DEFINER and RLS

The function `generate_meter_pm_work_orders` SHALL be `SECURITY DEFINER` because it inserts into `work_orders`, which has RLS policies restricting INSERT to PLANNER/ADMIN. As a trigger-fired function running behind an INSERT on `meter_readings` (which TECHNICIAN can perform), it needs elevated privileges.

The trigger SHALL run as the table owner (typically the migration user or database owner).

#### Scenario: TECHNICIAN inserts reading triggers WO creation

- GIVEN a TECHNICIAN user inserts a meter reading via the app
- WHEN the insert triggers `generate_meter_pm_work_orders()`
- THEN the function SHALL successfully create a WO even though TECHNICIAN does not have direct WO INSERT privileges

## Non-Functional Requirements

- **Idempotency**: All ALTER TABLE statements MUST use IF NOT EXISTS. Function MUST use CREATE OR REPLACE. Trigger MUST use DROP IF EXISTS + CREATE.
- **Performance**: The function SHALL use indexed queries (`idx_pm_schedules_asset`, new index on `pm_schedules.meter_id`).
- **Dedup integrity**: The dedup check MUST be atomic (within the same transaction as the WO INSERT) to prevent race conditions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `pm_schedules` has `meter_id` (FK→meters), `meter_trigger_value` (NUMERIC), `meter_reset_on_completion` (BOOLEAN DEFAULT false)
- [ ] `generate_meter_pm_work_orders()` exists, SECURITY DEFINER, returns INT
- [ ] Function correctly filters by meter_id, checks threshold, checks frequency window
- [ ] Dedup: same schedule does not produce duplicate WOs in same meter window
- [ ] `trg_meter_reading_pm_trigger` fires AFTER INSERT on `meter_readings`
- [ ] All migration statements are idempotent
- [ ] pgTAP tests cover 6+ scenarios

observations.title: sdd/meter-based-pm-trigger/design
observations.content:
# Design: Meter-Based PM Trigger

## Technical Approach

Single idempotent migration (`supabase/migrations/20260609000001_meter_based_pm_trigger.sql`) with three sections: (1) ALTER `pm_schedules` with meter-trigger columns, (2) `generate_meter_pm_work_orders()` SECURITY DEFINER function, (3) `trg_meter_reading_pm_trigger` on `meter_readings` AFTER INSERT. The meter-based pipeline is event-driven (trigger on INSERT), completely independent from the calendar-based `generate_due_preventive_work_orders()` which runs via pg_cron. Dedup is handled by checking `work_orders` for existing WOs matching the same schedule within the current meter window.

## Architecture Decisions

### Decision: Separate function (not merged into calendar PM engine)

| Option | Tradeoff | Decision |
|--------|----------|----------|
| Merge into `generate_due_preventive_work_orders()` | Single entry point but function must handle both trigger context and scheduled context; complicates testing | ❌ Rejected |
| Separate `generate_meter_pm_work_orders()` called from trigger | Clean separation of concerns; each function has one job; both are independently testable | ✅ **Chosen** |

**Rationale**: Meter-based PM is event-driven (trigger on `meter_readings` INSERT), while calendar-based is scheduled (pg_cron). Merging creates a function that needs to detect calling context (trigger vs. scheduled) — a design smell. Separate functions align with the single-responsibility principle.

### Decision: SECURITY DEFINER on function

| Option | Tradeoff | Decision |
|--------|----------|----------|
| SECURITY INVOKER | Trigger runs as TECHNICIAN who inserted reading; TECHNICIAN lacks INSERT on `work_orders` → WO creation fails | ❌ Rejected |
| SECURITY DEFINER | Function runs as owner; can insert into `work_orders` regardless of caller's RLS | ✅ **Chosen** |

**Rationale**: The trigger fires when a TECHNICIAN inserts a meter reading. TECHNICIAN has INSERT on `meter_readings` but NOT on `work_orders` (only PLANNER/ADMIN do). For the trigger to create WOs, the function must elevate privileges via SECURITY DEFINER. This is a broadly used pattern already established in the codebase (`generate_due_preventive_work_orders()` is already SECURITY DEFINER).

### Decision: Dedup via work_orders lookup (not a separate tracking table)

| Option | Tradeoff | Decision |
|--------|----------|----------|
| New `pm_schedule_triggers` tracking table | Clean audit trail but adds schema overhead, syncing complexity | ❌ Rejected |
| Query `work_orders` existing rows | No new tables; reuses existing WO schema; dedup accuracy depends on `last_completion_date` | ✅ **Chosen** |

**Rationale**: The existing `work_orders` table already has `job_plan_id`, `asset_id`, and `reported_at`. The dedup check queries: does a WO exist with the same `job_plan_id` + `asset_id` where `reported_at >= schedule.last_completion_date`? If yes, skip. This avoids a new tracking table while being accurate for the trigger window. Edge case: if no WO exists but the schedule hasn't been reset, we re-check the meter reading window.

### Decision: Pure SQL trigger (no Edge Function)

| Option | Tradeoff | Decision |
|--------|----------|----------|
| Edge Function + webhook | Async, decoupled, can do complex processing | ❌ Rejected |
| Pure SQL trigger | Synchronous but simple, no infra overhead, same transaction | ✅ **Chosen** |

**Rationale**: The function logic is pure SQL (query schedules → check thresholds → insert WO). Adding an Edge Function introduces deployment complexity, async consistency concerns, and latency for a task that completes in <10ms in SQL. For Phase 1, pure SQL is sufficient. An Edge Function wrapper can be added in Phase 2 if async processing (e.g., notifications, Epicor integration) becomes necessary.

## Data Flow

```
meter_readings INSERT
       │
       ▼
trg_meter_reading_pm_trigger (AFTER INSERT, FOR EACH ROW)
       │
       ▼
generate_meter_pm_work_orders(NEW.meter_id, NEW.reading_value)
       │
       ├─ 1. Query pm_schedules WHERE meter_id = p_meter_id
       │         AND meter_trigger_value IS NOT NULL
       │         AND p_reading_value >= meter_trigger_value
       │
       ├─ 2. For each match:
       │      ├─ Check frequency window (meter_frequency_value)
       │      ├─ Dedup check: EXISTS in work_orders? (job_plan_id + asset_id + reported_at)
       │      ├─ INSERT into work_orders (wo_type='PM', lifecycle_phase='WAPPR')
       │      └─ UPDATE pm_schedules (last_completion_date = NOW())
       │
       └─ 3. RETURN count of WOs created
```

## File Changes

| File | Action | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `supabase/migrations/20260609000001_meter_based_pm_trigger.sql` | Create | Single migration: ALTER pm_schedules, CREATE FUNCTION, CREATE TRIGGER |
| `supabase/tests/database/meter_based_pm_trigger_test.sql` | Create | pgTAP tests for all scenarios |
| `openspec/changes/meter-based-pm-trigger/design.md` | Create | This design document |

## Interfaces / Contracts

### SQL Function Signature

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION generate_meter_pm_work_orders(
  p_meter_id UUID,
  p_reading_value NUMERIC
)
RETURNS INT
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public
```

### pm_schedules — New Columns

```sql
ALTER TABLE pm_schedules
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS meter_id UUID REFERENCES meters(id),
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS meter_trigger_value NUMERIC,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS meter_reset_on_completion BOOLEAN DEFAULT false;
```

### Trigger

```sql
DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_meter_reading_pm_trigger ON meter_readings;
CREATE TRIGGER trg_meter_reading_pm_trigger
  AFTER INSERT ON meter_readings
  FOR EACH ROW
  EXECUTE FUNCTION generate_meter_pm_work_orders();
```

### Index

```sql
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_pm_schedules_meter ON pm_schedules(meter_id)
  WHERE meter_id IS NOT NULL;
```

### Dedup Query Pattern

```sql
IF EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM work_orders wo
  WHERE wo.job_plan_id = v_schedule.job_plan_id
    AND wo.asset_id = v_schedule.asset_id
    AND wo.reported_at >= COALESCE(v_schedule.last_completion_date, '1970-01-01'::TIMESTAMPTZ)
) THEN
  CONTINUE;  -- Skip, already have a WO in this window
END IF;
```

## Testing Strategy

| Layer | What to Test | Approach |
|-------|-------------|----------|
| Integration | ALTER TABLE adds columns correctly | Run migration against test DB, verify column metadata |
| Integration | FK constraint on meter_id | Insert invalid meter_id → expect FK violation |
| Unit (pgTAP) | Function with matching reading | Call function with reading >= threshold → expect 1 WO created |
| Unit (pgTAP) | Function with sub-threshold reading | Call with reading < threshold → expect 0 |
| Unit (pgTAP) | Dedup guard | Call twice with same args → expect 1 WO total |
| Unit (pgTAP) | Multiple schedules on same meter | Two schedules on same meter trigger → expect 2 WOs |
| Unit (pgTAP) | Frequency window check | Call with reading inside frequency window → expect 0 |
| Integration | Trigger fires on INSERT | Insert meter reading → verify WO created via trigger |
| Integration | RLS/SECURITY DEFINER | Insert as TECHNICIAN → verify WO created despite RLS |

## Migration / Rollout

**Migration order in file**: ALTER pm_schedules → CREATE INDEX → CREATE FUNCTION → CREATE TRIGGER. Triggers at the end because they depend on the function, which depends on the columns.

**Rollback**:
```sql
DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_meter_reading_pm_trigger ON meter_readings;
DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS generate_meter_pm_work_orders;
ALTER TABLE pm_schedules DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS meter_id;
ALTER TABLE pm_schedules DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS meter_trigger_value;
ALTER TABLE pm_schedules DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS meter_reset_on_completion;
```

**Idempotency**: All statements use IF EXISTS / OR REPLACE / IF NOT EXISTS. Safe to run repeatedly.

## Open Questions

- None. Spec, proposal, and design are aligned.

observations.title: sdd/meter-based-pm-trigger/tasks
observations.content:
**What**: Task breakdown for Meter-Based PM Trigger change — 3 phases: migration, testing, edge function (deferred)
**Why**: Enable usage-based preventive maintenance where work orders generate when a meter reading crosses a configured threshold
**Where**: `openspec/changes/meter-based-pm-trigger/tasks.md`, `supabase/migrations/20260609000001_meter_pm_trigger.sql`, `supabase/tests/database/meter_pm_trigger_test.sql`

## Phase 1: Migration (5 tasks)

1.1 ALTER pm_schedules: ADD meter_id UUID REFERENCES meters(id), meter_trigger_value NUMERIC, meter_reset_on_completion BOOLEAN DEFAULT false
1.2 CREATE generate_meter_pm_work_orders() — SECURITY DEFINER, queries schedules by meter_id, checks threshold + frequency window, inserts WOs, returns INT
1.3 CREATE TRIGGER trg_meter_reading_pm_trigger ON meter_readings AFTER INSERT FOR EACH ROW
1.4 CREATE INDEX idx_pm_schedules_meter_id ON pm_schedules(meter_id) WHERE meter_id IS NOT NULL
1.5 COMMENT on new columns, function, and trigger

## Phase 2: Testing (7 tasks)

2.1 Test: new columns exist on pm_schedules (has_column, col_is_fk, col_has_default)
2.2 Test: FK constraint — invalid meter_id raises violation
2.3 Test: trigger fires on INSERT into meter_readings and creates WO
2.4 Test: sub-threshold reading creates zero WOs
2.5 Test: dedup via work_orders lookup prevents duplicate WO
2.6 Test: meter_reset_on_completion re-trigger behavior
2.7 Test: SECURITY DEFINER — TECHNICIAN triggers WO creation

## Phase 3: Edge Function (deferred — 1 task noted, not in scope)

observations.title: TAREA: Exponer lifecycle_phase de work_orders para produccion-ibarra
observations.content:
**What**: TAREA para el equipo cmms-ibero: exponer el lifecycle_phase real de las work_orders para que la app de producción (produccion-ibarra) pueda mostrar el estado de las OTs generadas por el oee-trigger.

**Why**: Hoy produccion-ibarra dispara OEs correctivas vía oee-trigger, pero no puede ver si ya están aprobadas, en progreso, o completadas. Necesitan mostrar el estado real en la pantalla de conciliación.

**Datos que necesita produccion-ibarra**:
- `lifecycle_phase` (WAPPR/APPROVED/INPRG/COMP/CLOSED)
- `symptom_note` (el diagnóstico del operador)
- `cause_note` (diagnóstico del mecánico)
- `actual_start_at`, `completed_at` (cuándo se trabajó)
- `assigned_to` (técnico asignado)

**Mecanismo**: La colección `work_orders` ya se sincroniza vía GraphQL/Hasura entre ambos proyectos. Solo hay que asegurar que los campos nuevos estén disponibles en el schema de Hasura y en la respuesta GraphQL.

**Lo que debe cambiar en cmms-ibero**:
1. Verificar que `lifecycle_phase`, `symptom_note`, `cause_note`, `actual_start_at`, `completed_at`, `assigned_to`, `planned_hours` estén trackeados en Hasura metadata
2. Verificar que la consulta GraphQL `work_orders` incluya estos campos
3. Si algún campo no existe migrarlo (en la tabla `work_orders` ya deberían estar)
4. No necesita nuevas tablas ni edge functions — solo exposición de datos existentes

**Dependencia**: produccion-ibarra actualizará su schema de RxDB y DTO para consumir estos campos tan pronto estén disponibles en Hasura.

observations.title: Implemented meter-based-pm-trigger change
observations.content:
**What**: Implemented meter-based PM trigger — new pm_schedules columns, SECURITY DEFINER function, trigger on meter_readings INSERT, pgTAP tests
**Why**: Enable usage-based preventive maintenance (e.g., "Every 500 hours") independent of calendar-based PM engine
**Where**: supabase/migrations/20260609000001_meter_pm_trigger.sql (created), supabase/tests/database/meter_pm_trigger_test.sql (created), openspec/changes/meter-based-pm-trigger/tasks.md (updated)
**Learned**: 
- PostgreSQL does NOT support passing NEW.* as arguments in CREATE TRIGGER EXECUTE FUNCTION. Required a two-function approach: core function RETURNS INT with params, trigger wrapper RETURNS TRIGGER that extracts NEW values and delegates
- MAX() does not work on UUID type — used ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1 instead for frequency window logic
- $6$ meter_reset_on_completion$ needs NOT NULL DEFAULT false constraint per spec
- All 15 pgTAP tests passing: schema validation, FK constraint, direct function call, trigger firing, sub-threshold, frequency window, dedup, SECURITY DEFINER

observations.title: Session summary: cmms-ibero
observations.content:
## Goal
Implement change "meter-based-pm-trigger" — add meter-trigger columns to pm_schedules, create SECURITY DEFINER function, create AFTER INSERT trigger on meter_readings, and pgTAP tests.

## Instructions

## Goal

## Instructions

- Store híbrido (openspec + engram)
- Backend-first: features sin frontend se priorizan

## Discoveries
- **Trigger function architecture**: PostgreSQL NO permite pasar NEW.* como argumentos en CREATE TRIGGER EXECUTE FUNCTION. Una función que retorna INT no puede ser trigger function (debe retornar TRIGGER). Solución: dos funciones — una core (INT, llamable directamente) y una wrapper (TRIGGER).
- **NEW no disponible en función parametrizada**: La función `generate_meter_pm_work_orders()` recibe parámetros (no trigger context), así que NEW no existe. Para frequency window dedup, usar ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1.
- **GRANT SELECT ON ALL VIEWS IN SCHEMA**: PostgreSQL NO soporta esta sintaxis. Per-view grants necesarias.
- **epicor_outbox no tiene entity_type/entity_id**: Usar event_type + payload existentes, matching patrón enqueue_material_request().
- **pg_cron schedule necesita pg_net**: Si pg_net no está instalado, la schedule falla en runtime (la migración registra el cron exitosamente).
- **Edge Functions como stubs**: query-epicor-stock, create-epicor-pr, send-certification-reminder — todas creadas como stubs hasta tener API details de Epicor/canal de notificaciones.

observations.title: Seasonal scheduling design
observations.content:
**What**: Technical design for seasonal scheduling: WHERE clause additions in due_chain CTE (seasonal month check + blackout BETWEEN), advance logic as CASE expression in next_target_date UPDATE. No new functions, no new tables — purely additive to existing PM engine
**Why**: Minimal surface area, backward compatible, single migration
**Where**: openspec/changes/seasonal-scheduling/design.md
**Learned**: Year-wrapping inline logic pattern: (start <= end AND m BETWEEN start AND end) OR (start > end AND (m >= start OR m <= end)). Advance uses MAKE_DATE with year+1. The function signature stays unchanged.

## Goal
Implement the "job-plan-versioning" change: job_plan_revisions table, triggers for version auto-increment and revision archiving, work_order_skill_snapshots table, PM engine extension, backfill, RLS, and full pgTAP test suite.

## Instructions
- Follow Strict TDD mode — write tests first, then migration
- All SQL must be idempotent (IF NOT EXISTS, OR REPLACE, ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING)
- Use SECURITY DEFINER for triggers that cross ownership boundaries

## Discoveries
- PM engine function needed full `CREATE OR REPLACE` to add the skill snapshot section — cannot modify in place
- pgTAP savepoint failures can silently prevent later assertions from running if an unhandled exception occurs within a savepoint; use DO blocks to isolate function calls that might raise exceptions
- UUID values in pgTAP tests must be valid 36-char format (8-4-4-4-12 hex digits). Shorter or non-hex characters cause `invalid input syntax for type uuid` errors
- `row_to_json()` with `::jsonb` cast works cleanly for building composite JSONB snapshots from relational rows

observations.title: sdd/wo-lifecycle-outbox/proposal
observations.content:
# Proposal: WO Lifecycle Outbox — Production Status Push

## Intent

Production tablets and conciliation screens in produccion-ibarra need real-time MTTO intervention status. When `lifecycle_phase` changes in cmms-ibero (e.g., INPRG→COMP), that transition must push asynchronously so produccion-ibarra displays accurate maintenance status without polling or manual entry.

## Scope

### In Scope
- `enqueue_work_order_lifecycle()` trigger on `work_orders` AFTER UPDATE → `epicor_outbox`
- Edge Function `push-workorder-status` polls outbox, POSTs to produccion-ibarra
- produccion-ibarra schema extension (lifecycle columns + `cmms_wo_id`)
- produccion-ibarra GraphQL schema + RxDB schema update
- ConciliationScreen UI — lifecycle_phase badge

### Out of Scope
- Bidirectional sync (produccion→cmms)
- Epicor or stock integration
- Historical backfill
- Editing lifecycle fields from produccion-ibarra (read-only)
- Analytics on MTTO times

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities
- `wo-lifecycle-push`: Cross-system status push via Transactional Outbox

### Modified Capabilities
- `procurement-integration/epicor_outbox`: New event_type `WORK_ORDER_LIFECYCLE` added (table unchanged)
- `mechanic-work-order-execution`: produccion-ibarra gains lifecycle visibility

## Approach

Push-based Transactional Outbox. AFTER UPDATE trigger on `work_orders` inserts into `epicor_outbox` (reuse existing table). Edge Function `push-workorder-status` polls for `event_type='WORK_ORDER_LIFECYCLE'` AND `status='PENDING'` AND `next_retry_at<=NOW()`, sends HTTP POST to Hasura REST endpoint on produccion-ibarra with Bearer token auth, then marks SENT/FAILED. produccion-ibarra resolves by `cmms_wo_id`, updates columns. Single event type — payload carries the new lifecycle_phase value.

## Affected Areas

| Area | Impact | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| cmms-ibero DB | New | Trigger + func `enqueue_work_order_lifecycle()` |
| `supabase/functions/push-workorder-status/` | New | Edge Function polling outbox |
| `supabase/tests/database/` | New | pgTAP tests |
| produccion-ibarra DB | Modified | ALTER work_orders ADD COLUMNS |
| produccion-ibarra GraphQL | Modified | IWorkOrder + RxDB + pull query |
| produccion-ibarra UI | Modified | ConciliationScreen lifecycle badge |

## Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|------|------------|------------|
| Destination down | Medium | Retry via epicor_outbox retry_count + next_retry_at |
| Duplicate on retry | Low | Idempotent — same phase update is no-op |
| Schema mismatch | Low | `cmms_wo_id` avoids PK conflict; migration first |

## Rollback Plan

Drop trigger + function. Remove `push-workorder-status` Edge Function. Revert produccion-ibarra migration (DROP COLUMNS). Outbox events remain for reprocessing. No data loss.

## Dependencies

observations.title: sdd/wo-lifecycle-outbox/design
observations.content:
# Design: WO Lifecycle Outbox — Production Status Push

## Technical Approach

Transactional Outbox pattern: AFTER UPDATE trigger on `work_orders` inserts into existing `epicor_outbox` with `event_type='WORK_ORDER_LIFECYCLE'`. A new Edge Function `push-workorder-status` polls the outbox, POSTs to produccion-ibarra's Hasura REST endpoint, and marks SENT/FAILED with exponential backoff. Produccion-ibarra upserts by `cmms_wo_id` and syncs to tablets via RxDB.

## Architecture Decisions

### Table reuse vs. new outbox table
- **Reuse `epicor_outbox`** with `event_type='WORK_ORDER_LIFECYCLE'` — same status FSM, retry, indexing
- Rejected: separate table (duplicates boilerplate) or one-per-event-type (over-engineered)

### Push via Edge Function vs. pg_cron direct HTTP
- **Edge Function** polling — matches existing `create-epicor-pr` pattern, testable, env-var config
- Rejected: pg_cron+pg_net (harder to debug/test/auth)

### Single payload snapshot vs. minimal delta
- **Full row snapshot** — same JSONB for all phases, consumer picks what it needs. Simpler.

## Data Flow

```
work_orders UPDATE ──→ epicor_outbox (trigger insert, PENDING)
                        └── push-workorder-status (poll every 1min)
                              └── POST /api/rest/upsert-work-order-lifecycle
                                    → Hasura → work_orders upsert by cmms_wo_id
                                    → RxDB sync → Tablet ConciliationScreen UI
```

## Component Specifications

### 1. Trigger [cmms-ibero] — `enqueue_work_order_lifecycle()`
- AFTER UPDATE on work_orders, WHEN lifecycle_phase IS DISTINCT FROM OLD
- Inserts epicor_outbox (event_type='WORK_ORDER_LIFECYCLE', payload=jsonb_build_object of 13 fields: id, asset_id, equipment_id, wo_type, lifecycle_phase, block_reason, symptom_note, cause_note, action_note, actual_start_at, completed_at, planned_hours, updated_at)
- Runs AFTER BEFORE UPDATE triggers (FSM validates first, status syncs second)

### 2. Edge Function [cmms-ibero] — `push-workorder-status`
- Same pattern as create-epicor-pr: polling query, PROCESSING→SENT/FAILED FSM
- Auth: `x-hasura-admin-secret` header from env PRODUCCION_HASURA_SECRET
- Target URL from env PRODUCCION_HASURA_URL
- Backoff: `NOW() + LEAST(INTERVAL '24h', (2^retry_count) * INTERVAL '1 min')`
- Dead letter after 10 retries (status=FAILED permanent)
- deno.json imports @supabase/supabase-js, config.toml verify_jwt=false

### 3. Schema migration [produccion] — ALTER work_orders
- ADD cmms_wo_id TEXT UNIQUE, lifecycle_phase TEXT, block_reason TEXT DEFAULT 'NONE', symptom_note TEXT, cause_note TEXT, actual_start_at TIMESTAMPTZ, completed_at TIMESTAMPTZ
- CREATE INDEX idx_work_orders_cmms_wo_id

### 4. Hasura REST endpoint [produccion]
- POST /api/rest/upsert-work-order-lifecycle
- Auth: x-hasura-admin-secret
- GraphQL: insert_work_orders on_conflict { constraint: work_orders_cmms_wo_id_key, update_columns: [lifecycle_phase, block_reason, symptom_note, cause_note, actual_start_at, completed_at] }

### 5. IWorkOrder + RxDB [produccion]
- types.ts: add 7 optional fields to interface
- schemas.ts: bump RxDB schema version, add new fields
- dto.ts: map all 7 fields in GraphQLWorkOrder
- sync.ts: include new fields in GraphQL selection set

### 6. ConciliationScreen UI [produccion]
- Badge showing lifecycle_phase with color mapping: WAPPR(gray), APPROVED(blue), INPRG(orange), COMP(green), CLOSED(teal), CANCELLED(red), REJECTED(red)

## Migration Order
1. produccion: ALTER + INDEX (MUST be first)
2. produccion: Hasura REST endpoint
3. produccion: IWorkOrder + RxDB + GraphQL updates
4. cmms-ibero: trigger migration
5. cmms-ibero: Edge Function + cron (MUST be last)
6. produccion: ConciliationScreen UI

## Error Scenarios
- Network/auth failure → retry_count++, exponential backoff, up to 10×
- Schema mismatch → FAILED permanent (deployment order issue)
- Duplicate on retry → idempotent (same phase upsert = no-op)

## Open Questions
- Confirm produccion-ibarra's Hasura URL and Nhost instance
- Verify constraint name for cmms_wo_id unique
- Dead-letter alerting strategy (currently silent)

observations.title: sdd/condition-monitoring-phase-1/proposal
observations.content:
# Proposal: Condition Monitoring — Phase 1

## Intent

Build the ingestion and governance layer for condition-based maintenance — receive IIoT sensor features from edge, store with quality-gated EAV catalog, compute authoritative Health Index, and generate CBM work orders. Architecture principle: "El edge mide, el CMMS decide."

## Scope

### In Scope
- `condition_feature_definitions` catalog (EAV control)
- `condition_windows` + `condition_feature_values` (quality-gated, denormalized)
- `condition_events` (on-trigger only)
- Edge Function `ingest-condition` (POST FeatureSet v0.2, continuous)
- Edge Function `ingest-events` (POST events, on-trigger)
- `compute_health_index()` SQL function (weighted HI + dHI/dt)
- Extend CBM trigger `evaluate_meter_reading_for_cbm()` for HI-based WO generation
- pgTAP tests for schema, functions, triggers, EF validation

### Out of Scope
- Dashboards/UI (Phase 2)
- RUL prediction (Phase 3)
- Advanced diagnostics/ML (Phase 3)
- Multi-tenant isolation
- Raw artifact storage (edge retains high-frequency data)
- Calibration management (G0–G3 flags suffice)
- Mobile app changes

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities
- `condition-data-ingest`: HTTP ingestion of FeatureSet v0.2 — validates against catalog, stores windows and feature values with per-row quality flags, rejects unmapped feature keys
- `condition-health-index`: Computes authoritative HI from weighted normalized features with configurable weights, exposes dHI/dt degradation velocity
- `condition-events`: Manages triggered condition events (alarms, threshold breaches, diagnostic flags) separate from continuous feature ingestion

### Modified Capabilities
- `preventive-condition-core`: Extend `evaluate_meter_reading_for_cbm()` trigger to also evaluate HI-based thresholds and auto-generate CBM work orders from `condition_events`
- `mechanic-work-order-execution`: Add HI data fields to WO data contract (data layer only; UI rendering in drawer deferred to Phase 2)

## Approach

EAV-controlled by `condition_feature_definitions` catalog to prevent free-text garbage. `measurement_point_id` per feature row (not in header). Denormalized `asset_id` + `window_start` in feature_values for query perf. Two Edge Functions following proven `oee-trigger` pattern. HI on CMMS is authoritative; edge HI (hi_tentative) is real-time only. Extend existing CBM generation logic — do not replace it.

## Affected Areas

| Area | Impact | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `supabase/migrations/` | New | 4 tables, indexes, `compute_health_index()`, COMMENT ON |
| `supabase/functions/ingest-condition/` | New | Edge Function: POST /rest/v1/condition_features |
| `supabase/functions/ingest-events/` | New | Edge Function: POST /rest/v1/condition_events |
| CBM trigger function | Modified | Extend for HI thresholds |
| `supabase/config.toml` | Modified | Function routes, JWT config |
| `supabase/tests/database/` | New | pgTAP: schema, functions, triggers, EF behavior |

## Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|------|------------|------------|
| Edge sends malformed FeatureSet | Med | EF validates shape + catalog FK; G3 flags bad data |
| High ingestion rate impacts perf | Med | Indexed window_start; EF batches writes |
| HI dependency on missing features | Low | Missing features treated as 0 contribution; HI degrades gracefully |

## Rollback Plan

DROP 4 new tables, DROP `compute_health_index()`, revert CBM trigger to previous version, remove both Edge Functions, revert `config.toml`. Append-only data — no loss if rolled back within 24h.

## Dependencies

- `preventive-condition-core` schema (meters, measure_points, CBM trigger)
- `oee-trigger` Edge Function pattern (HTTP ingestion reference)
- IIoT team delivery of FeatureSet v0.2 contract

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Edge POSTs FeatureSet → data persisted in `condition_windows` + `condition_feature_values` with correct quality flags
- [ ] `compute_health_index()` returns correct weighted HI for known feature vectors
