observations.title: Proposal: Condition Monitoring — Phase 2
observations.content:
# Proposal: Condition Monitoring — Phase 2

## Intent

Extend Phase 1 ingestion + HI core with threshold management (multiple sets per feature), operational regime normalization, time-decay for stale data, health trend queries, hierarchical HI aggregation, metrological correction (Kalman), and event lifecycle enhancements.

## Scope

### In Scope
- Thresholds configuration API — populate reference_normal/reference_critical, multiple sets per feature (by asset class, model, per-asset)
- Operational regime normalization — match threshold set by load_pct/regime from condition_windows.operational_context
- Time-decay for stale features — reduce HI contribution proportionally to elapsed time since last reading
- get_health_trend(p_asset_id, p_interval) — time-series HI function
- Hierarchical HI — asset → system → plant aggregation weighted by criticality
- Corrección metrológica — moving average / exponential smoothing; Kalman as stretch goal
- Event status lifecycle — OPEN → linked_to_wo → CLOSED → dismissed (plus manual acknowledge). Auto-close when WO reaches CLOSED.

### Out of Scope
- RUL prediction or ML diagnostics (Phase 3)
- Dashboards / UI (separate change)
- Raw artifact storage (edge retains high-freq data)
- Multi-tenant isolation

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities
- None — all changes modify existing capabilities

### Modified Capabilities
- condition-health-index: Threshold sets per feature + regime matching + time-decay + hierarchical HI + metrological correction
- condition-events: Extended status lifecycle (linked_to_wo, dismissed), auto-close on WO CLOSED

## Approach

Threshold sets via new condition_feature_thresholds table (FK → condition_feature_definitions), with asset_type_id, asset_id, load_pct_min/max, rpm_min/max columns for regime matching. update_feature_references() upserts into this table. compute_health_index() queries active threshold set matching current operating context, falls back to feature definition defaults. Time-decay as weight * EXP(-elapsed_seconds / decay_constant). Hierarchical HI via recursive CTE over asset_hierarchy weighted by criticality. Event status CHECK expanded from 3 to 5 states; auto-close via AFTER UPDATE trigger on work_orders.

## Affected Areas

| Area | Impact | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| supabase/migrations/ | New | Thresholds table, HI rewrite, trend function, event lifecycle, Kalman filter (stretch) |
| supabase/functions/ingest-condition/ | Modified | Metrological correction pre-processing |
| compute_health_index() | Modified | Regime matching + time-decay + hierarchical aggregation |
| get_health_trend() | New | Time-series HI function |
| trg_condition_event_to_wo | Modified | Status transition auto-close logic |
| supabase/tests/database/ | New | pgTAP for thresholds, trend, regime, decay, hierarchy, event lifecycle |

## Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|------|------------|------------|
| Regime matching adds HI latency | Med | Index threshold_sets by (feature_key, asset_type_id); short-circuit exact match |
| Hierarchical HI perf on deep trees | Low | Materialized path in asset_hierarchy; limit recursion |
| Kalman filter complexity | Med | Defer to stretch; ship exponential smoothing first |

## Rollback Plan

DROP condition_feature_thresholds, rollback compute_health_index() to Phase 1, revert event status CHECK, DROP get_health_trend(). Append-only — safe within 24h.

## Dependencies
- Phase 1 schema (4 tables, HI function, CBM trigger)
- asset_hierarchy table for hierarchical HI
- asset_types table for class-based matching
- IIoT team agreement on regime metadata

## Success Criteria
- [ ] update_feature_references() creates/updates threshold sets; regime matching selects correct set
- [ ] Stale feature shows reduced HI via time-decay
- [ ] get_health_trend('A1', '7 days') returns ordered time series
- [ ] Hierarchical HI: system-level = weighted avg of child HIs
- [ ] Event transitions: OPEN → linked_to_wo → CLOSED (auto); dismissed from any non-CLOSED
- [ ] All pgTAP tests pass (existing 57 + new assertions)

observations.title: Design: Condition Monitoring Phase 2
observations.content:
**What**: Technical design for Condition Monitoring Phase 2 — thresholds, regime matching, time-decay, trend queries, hierarchical HI, EWMA correction, event lifecycle (5 states, auto-close on WO CLOSED)

**Why**: Extend Phase 1 ingestion+HI core to production-grade CM analytics with configurable thresholds, stale-data handling, and hierarchical aggregation

**Where**: openspec/changes/condition-monitoring-phase-2/design.md, engram sdd/condition-monitoring-phase-2/design

**Learned**: 
- Keep reference_normal/critical on condition_feature_definitions as fallback; new condition_feature_thresholds table overrides via priority chain (asset_id > asset_type_id > model > default)
- Regime matching queries operational_context JSONB directly (no schema change to condition_windows needed)
- Time-decay uses EXP(-elapsed_seconds / 86400) per-feature multiplicative factor
- Hierarchical HI via recursive CTE over existing asset_hierarchy weighted by assets.criticality (A=3, B=2, C=1)
- EWMA chosen over Kalman for metrological correction — Kalman deferred to stretch goal
- Event status expanded from 3 to 5 states: open, acknowledged, linked_to_wo, closed, dismissed
- Auto-close via AFTER UPDATE trigger on work_orders checking lifecycle_phase = 'CLOSED' AND condition_event_id IS NOT NULL
- 4 migrations planned: thresholds table, HI rewrite, event lifecycle, EWMA column

observations.title: sdd/condition-monitoring-phase-2/spec
observations.content:
# Condition Monitoring Phase 2 — Delta Specifications

## Domain: condition-data-ingest

### ADDED: Feature Thresholds Table

The system MUST create a `condition_feature_thresholds` table storing multiple threshold sets per feature definition. Each set SHALL define `reference_normal` and `reference_critical` values with optional regime and asset-type scoping.

Columns: id (UUID PK), feature_key (FK→condition_feature_definitions), asset_type_id (FK→asset_types, nullable), asset_id (FK→assets, nullable), load_pct_min/max (nullable), rpm_min/max (nullable), reference_normal (NOT NULL), reference_critical (NOT NULL), is_active (BOOLEAN DEFAULT true), created_at. UNIQUE on (feature_key, asset_type_id, asset_id, load_pct_min, load_pct_max, rpm_min, rpm_max).

**Scenarios**: Create class-level set, create per-asset override, duplicate rejected.

### ADDED: `update_feature_references()` Function

PL/pgSQL upsert function for threshold sets. Signature: `update_feature_references(p_feature_key, p_asset_type_id DEFAULT NULL, p_asset_id DEFAULT NULL, p_load_pct_min/max DEFAULT NULL, p_rpm_min/max DEFAULT NULL, p_reference_normal, p_reference_critical) RETURNS UUID`. Uses INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE on the unique constraint.

**Scenarios**: Creates new set, updates existing set, unknown feature_key raises FK error.

## Domain: condition-health-index

### ADDED: Regime-Matched Threshold Selection

HI computation SHALL select most specific matching threshold set per feature. Resolution order: (1) per-asset + regime match → (2) per-asset no regime → (3) class + regime match → (4) class no regime → (5) feature definition defaults.

**Scenarios**: Per-asset preferred over class, regime-matched set selected based on load_pct, fallback to feature definition when no threshold exists.

### ADDED: Hierarchical HI Aggregation

`compute_hierarchical_hi(p_asset_id TEXT) RETURNS TABLE(asset_id TEXT, hi DOUBLE PRECISION, level TEXT)` — recursive CTE over asset_hierarchy weighted by criticality. Formula: SUM(hi_child * criticality) / SUM(criticality). Levels: 'plant' (root), 'system' (intermediate), 'asset' (leaf).

**Scenarios**: Two-child weighted average, leaf returns single row, child with no data contributes 0.

### ADDED: Metrological Correction (Exponential Smoothing)

Smoothed = previous_smoothed * alpha + raw * (1 - alpha). Column smoothing_alpha added to condition_feature_definitions (DEFAULT 0.3, range [0,1]). Applied inside compute_health_index().

**Scenarios**: Attenuates transient spike, no prior = use raw, alpha=1.0 disables.

### MODIFIED: HI Computation Formula

Normalization now uses matched threshold set (reference_normal/reference_critical) instead of feature definition defaults. Falls back to definition columns if no threshold set matches. (Previously: used only definition normal_min/normal_max)

### MODIFIED: Missing Feature Decay

Precise formula: decay_factor = EXP(-elapsed_seconds / decay_constant). Column decay_seconds added to condition_feature_definitions (DEFAULT 86400). Contribution = weight * normalized_value * decay_factor. (Previously: stated decay without formula)

**Scenarios**: 48h stale ~13.5% contribution, 10min fresh ~99.3%, no data = 0.

## Domain: condition-events

### ADDED: Event Dismissal

DISMISSED allowed from any non-CLOSED status. Terminal state — no further transitions.

**Scenarios**: Dismiss from OPEN, dismiss from linked_to_wo, dismiss from CLOSED rejected.

### ADDED: Auto-Close Events on WO Completion

AFTER UPDATE trigger on work_orders fires when lifecycle_phase→'CLOSED' AND condition_event_id IS NOT NULL. Sets event status to 'CLOSED'.

**Scenarios**: Auto-closes event, no-event WO does nothing, non-CLOSED transition does nothing.

### MODIFIED: `condition_events` Table

Status CHECK expanded to ('OPEN','ACKNOWLEDGED','linked_to_wo','CLOSED','DISMISSED'). (Previously: only 'OPEN','ACKNOWLEDGED','CLOSED')

### MODIFIED: Event Status Transitions

Lifecycle: OPEN → (ACKNOWLEDGED) → linked_to_wo → CLOSED. DISMISSED from any non-CLOSED. linked_to_wo on trigger WO creation. CLOSED on WO completion. (Previously: OPEN → ACKNOWLEDGED → CLOSED only)

### MODIFIED: `trg_condition_event_to_wo` (Updated Status)

After creating CBM WO, trigger now also sets event status to 'linked_to_wo'. (Previously: only created WO, didn't update event status)

**Scenarios**: High severity links event to WO, critical same, info does nothing.

observations.content:
# Delta for Condition Health Index

## ADDED Requirements
- **Regime-Matched Threshold Selection**: Resolution order (1) per-asset+regime → (2) per-asset → (3) class+regime → (4) class → (5) definition defaults. Matching via load_pct/rpm bounds.
- **Hierarchical HI Aggregation**: compute_hierarchical_hi() via recursive CTE, weighted by criticality. Levels: plant/system/asset.
- **Metrological Correction**: Exponential smoothing (alpha factor) applied inside compute_health_index(). Column smoothing_alpha added to condition_feature_definitions.

## MODIFIED Requirements
- **HI Computation Formula**: Normalization uses matched threshold reference_normal/reference_critical instead of definition-only defaults.
- **Missing Feature Decay**: Precise formula decay_factor = EXP(-elapsed_seconds / decay_constant). Column decay_seconds added to condition_feature_definitions (DEFAULT 86400).

**Files**: openspec/changes/condition-monitoring-phase-2/delta/condition-health-index/delta.md

## Completed Tasks

### Migration 1: Thresholds

### Migration 2: HI v2
- ✅ 2.1 Rewrote `compute_health_index()` with regime-matched threshold resolution (asset_id→asset_type_id→definition fallback) + p_hierarchy/p_regime params
- ✅ 2.2 Added time-decay: EXP(-elapsed_seconds / decay_seconds) per-feature multiplicative factor

### Migration 3: Event Lifecycle
- ✅ 3.1 CHECK constraint reaffirmed with linked_to_wo, dismissed, closed (already in 20260530000005)
- ✅ 3.2 Created `trg_condition_event_close_on_wo_closed()` — AFTER UPDATE on work_orders
- ✅ 3.3 `trg_condition_event_to_wo()` reaffirmed with linked_to_wo status (already in 20260530000005)

### Migration 4: EWMA Column
- ✅ 4.1 ALTER TABLE condition_feature_values ADD COLUMN ewma_value DOUBLE PRECISION

### Migration 5: Post-Verify Fixes (NEW)
- ✅ 5.1 ADD COLUMN `updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ` to `condition_events` + BEFORE UPDATE trigger (`set_condition_events_updated_at`) — auto-sets on any UPDATE
- ✅ 5.2 Created FSM enforcement trigger (`trg_condition_event_status_fsm`) — BEFORE UPDATE on condition_events, valid transitions: open→{acknowledged,linked_to_wo,dismissed}, acknowledged→{linked_to_wo,closed}, linked_to_wo→{closed,dismissed}; terminal states: closed, dismissed
- ✅ 5.3 Updated auto-close trigger (`trg_condition_event_close_on_wo_closed`) — removed 'open' from allowed statuses to align with FSM (open→closed is invalid)

### Edge Function
- ✅ 6.1 Updated ingest-condition/index.ts: fetch smoothing_alpha, call fn_ewma_smooth() per feature

### pgTAP Tests
- ✅ 7.1 Thresholds test: CRUD, update_feature_references(), indexes, RLS
- ✅ 7.2 HI v2 test: regime matching, time-decay, hierarchy, trend, EWMA
- ✅ 7.3 Event lifecycle test: status transitions, auto-close, linked_to_wo
- ✅ 7.4 FSM enforcement tests: OPEN→acknowledged (valid), OPEN→CLOSED (rejected), CLOSED→dismissed (rejected terminal), DISMISSED→acknowledged (rejected terminal)

## Design Decisions (Post-Verify)
- `updated_at` is nullable (no DEFAULT) — the BEFORE UPDATE trigger sets it on any UPDATE. Existing rows get NULL until their first post-migration update.
- FSM trigger uses `WHEN (OLD.status IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.status)` — only fires when status actually changes, allowing non-status updates (e.g., diagnosis edits) without triggering FSM validation.
- Auto-close trigger excludes 'open' status. Events must be acknowledged or linked_to_wo before auto-close can transition to closed. This aligns with the FSM where open→closed is not valid.
- The FSM trigger and updated_at trigger are both BEFORE UPDATE. Alphabetical order: `trg_condition_event_status_fsm` runs first (validates), then `trg_condition_events_updated_at` (sets timestamp). If FSM rejects, the update is rolled back entirely.
- The `trg_condition_event_to_wo` trigger (AFTER INSERT) sets status to 'linked_to_wo' via UPDATE, which fires the FSM trigger — valid from 'open' (post-INSERT status).

observations.title: sdd/fmea-rcm-module/explore
observations.content:
## Exploration: FMEA/RCM Module Foundation

### Current State
The system tracks corrective work orders but has ZERO structured failure analysis. work_orders has ISO 14224 failure taxonomy columns (failure_class, problem_code, cause_code, remedy_code) but they are dead columns — never populated by the frontend. Only symptom_note, cause_note, action_note are filled by mechanics during INPRG→COMP transitions.

Asset model has flat assets with asset_hierarchy for plant structure. No component breakdown per asset. technological_modules (8 codes: M-PACK, M-TRAN, M-ELEC, M-REFR, M-VAPO, M-PUMP, M-TERM, M-INFR) map assets to technical domains.

Condition monitoring creates CBM WOs automatically via trg_condition_event_to_wo() when severity is high/critical, linking via condition_event_id. The causa_falla_catalog (6 codes) is about technician execution failure, NOT equipment failure — feeds competency engine.

Bi views layer is PM-only. Zero views for failure analysis, MTBF, MTTR, or component reliability.

### Key Design Answers
1. **Component hierarchy**: Flat asset_components table with component_types catalog (ISO 14224 codes). Cleaner than overloading asset_hierarchy.
2. **Failure mode catalog**: Separate failure_mode_catalog table keyed to component_type_id. Seed with ~200 ISO 14224 common modes, user-extensible via ADMIN/PLANNER UI.
3. **FMEA vs RCM**: Combined fmea_rcm_analysis table. FMEA feeds RCM naturally (RPN + 5 binary questions → maintenance strategy).
4. **WO close-out**: Mandatory lightweight step (3-4 dropdowns) at CLOSED for corrective/CBM WOs, plus standalone editor for reliability engineers.
5. **BI views**: 5 new views — v_fact_failure_occurrences, v_fact_mtbf, v_fact_mttr, v_fmea_high_rpn, mv_component_reliability_monthly.

### RCM Decision Tree
5 binary questions: has_pf_interval → causes_safety_env → causes_prod_loss → pm_is_feasible → detectable_tech
Strategies: BCM (predictive), PM (preventive), RTF (run-to-failure), REDESIGN

### Risks
1. Seed data quality — mitigate with ISO 14224 research + user extensibility
2. Mechanic friction — mitigate with 3-4 clicks + "unknown" option
3. No historical data — views show NULL/0 gracefully
4. RxDB complexity — follow checklist_instances replication pattern
5. RLS boilerplate — copy causa_falla_catalog RLS pattern

### Ready for Proposal: Yes

observations.title: sdd/fmea-rcm-module-sdd1/proposal
observations.content:
# Proposal: SDD 1 — Component Catalog + FMEA/RCM Analysis

## Intent

Database foundation for reliability engineering. Without component catalogs and structured failure analysis, MTBF/MTTR and reliability analytics are impossible.

## Scope

### In Scope
- `component_types` catalog (ISO 14224 codes: BEA, SEA, IMP, MTR)
- `asset_components` per asset (type FK, name, position, serial)
- `failure_mode_catalog` (per component type, ISO 14224 seeded, user-extensible)
- `fmea_rcm_analysis` table (S/O/D → RPN + 5 binary RCM questions → strategy)
- RCM tree: 32 combos → BCM/PM/RTF/REDESIGN via PL/pgSQL
- RxDB: 4 collections (pull-only catalogs, pull+push analysis)
- RLS: catalogs=SELECT all; analysis=own records (ADMIN=all)
- pgTAP tests: schema, constraints, RLS

### Out of Scope
- ❌ `failure_occurrences` & WO close-out (SDD 2)
- ❌ BI reliability views (SDD 3)
- ❌ UI for FMEA/RCM wizard (frontend)
- ❌ Historical data backfill

## Capabilities

### New
- `component-catalog`: `component_types` taxonomy + `asset_components` per asset
- `fmea-rcm-analysis`: `failure_mode_catalog` + `fmea_rcm_analysis` table + RCM decision tree

### Modified
- None — SDD 1 introduces new tables only; no existing spec behavior changes

## Approach

One migration: 4 tables, RCM function, RLS, seeds (~10 component types, ~50 failure modes). Combined `fmea_rcm_analysis` per exploration recommendation. RCM tree as PL/pgSQL CASE expression. RxDB replicators follow existing `checklist_instances` pattern. RLS via `get_user_role()` per auth-rbac spec.

## Affected Areas

| Area | Impact |
|------|--------|
| `supabase/migrations/` | New migration |
| `src/lib/rxdb.js` | +4 collections |
| `openspec/specs/component-catalog/` | New spec |
| `openspec/specs/fmea-rcm-analysis/` | New spec |
| `supabase/tests/database/` | New pgTAP suite |

## Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|------|------------|------------|
| Seed data quality | Med | ISO 14224 + research; user-extensible via ADMIN |
| RxDB replication complexity | Med | Follow `checklist_instances` pattern exactly |
| RLS policy gaps | Low | Template from `causa_falla_catalog`; 4-eyes on migration |

## Rollback

Single DOWN migration: DROP 4 tables, RCM function, any ENUMs. RxDB version check removes collections on next app load.

## Dependencies

None — all-new tables, no existing schema modifications.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] 4 tables created with correct FKs, constraints, `COMMENT ON`
- [ ] ≥10 component type seeds, ≥50 failure mode seeds
- [ ] RCM function returns correct strategy for all 32 question combinations
- [ ] RLS: TECHNICIAN = SELECT on catalogs, INSERT/UPDATE own analysis
- [ ] RLS: ADMIN = CRUD all analysis records
- [ ] pgTAP ≥20 passing tests
- [ ] RxDB pull-only replication for catalogs, pull+push for analysis

## Domain: Failure Mode Catalog

### Requirements

- User-extensible: ADMIN can INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, PLANNER can INSERT
- RLS: authenticated SELECT, PLANNER INSERT, ADMIN ALL

### Scenarios (7 total)
1. Insert failure mode for bearing
2. Duplicate code per type rejected
3. Same code allowed across different types
4. Deactivated mode excluded from UI
5. Seed count between 30–50
6. ADMIN adds custom failure mode
7. Technician insert rejected

## Domain: FMEA/RCM Analysis

Full spec at `openspec/changes/fmea-rcm-module/sdd1/specs/fmea-rcm-analysis/spec.md`

### Requirements
- `fmea_rcm_analysis` (id UUID PK, asset_id FK→assets CASCADE, component_id FK→asset_components CASCADE, failure_mode_id FK→failure_mode_catalog RESTRICT, severity 1-10, occurrence 1-10, detection 1-10, rpn computed S×O×D, 5 RCM boolean questions, recommended_strategy CHECK IN ('BCM','PM','RTF','REDESIGN'), notes, analyzed_by FK→auth.users, timestamps)
- UNIQUE(component_id, failure_mode_id)
- RCM decision tree: Q1→BCM, Q2+Q4→PM, Q2+¬Q4→REDESIGN, ¬Q2+Q3→PM, ¬Q2+¬Q3→RTF, Q2+¬Q4+Q5→BCM

2. Out-of-range severity rejected

6. RCM: no consequences → RTF

observations.title: sdd/fmea-rcm-module-sdd1/design
observations.content:
# Design: SDD 1 — Component Catalog + FMEA/RCM Analysis

## Technical Approach

Single migration `20260531000003_fmea_rcm_module_sdd1.sql` creating 4 tables, a
PL/pgSQL RCM decision function, seed data (10 component types, 38 failure
modes), RLS policies, and COMMENT ON in Spanish. RxDB schemas follow the
existing `checklist_instances` pattern. Catalogs are pull-only; analysis is
pull+push.

## Architecture Decisions

| # | Option | Choice | Rationale |
|---|--------|--------|-----------|
| 1 | FMEA/RCM combined vs separate | Combined `fmea_rcm_analysis` | FMEA feeds RCM naturally, single UI flow, fewer JOINs |
| 2 | RPN computation | Generated column rpn = S×O×D STORED | Cannot be wrong at app level; zero maintenance |
| 3 | RCM strategy | PL/pgSQL function fn_determine_rcm_strategy() with CASE | 32 combos → 4 strategies; trigger auto-computes on write |
| 4 | FK failure_mode_catalog deletion | RESTRICT from fmea_rcm_analysis | Prevents orphaned analysis referencing deleted failure modes |
| 5 | FK asset_components deletion | CASCADE from fmea_rcm_analysis | When a component is removed, its analyses go with it |
| 6 | Code constraint | CHECK (code ~ '^[A-Z_]+$') on component_types | Enforces uppercase ISO codes at DB level |
| 7 | RLS pattern | Named policies {tbl}_select/insert/update/delete | Matches existing competency_engine and checklist_evidence migrations |
| 8 | Failure mode codes | UNIQUE(component_type_id, failure_mode_code) | Same code reused across types (e.g., OVH for BEA and MTR) |
| 9 | Asset components | UNIQUE(asset_id, name) | No duplicate component names per asset |

## Data Flow

```
User → RxDB fmea_rcm_analysis → push → supabase/rest/v1/fmea_rcm_analysis
                                         → trigger → fn_determine_rcm_strategy()
                                         → pull → RxDB (with recommended_strategy)
Catalogs (pull-only): component_types, asset_components, failure_mode_catalog
```

## File Changes

| File | Action | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| supabase/migrations/20260531000003_fmea_rcm_module_sdd1.sql | Create | 4 tables + RCM function + RLS + seeds + comments |
| supabase/tests/database/..._test.sql | Create | pgTAP test suite (≥20 tests) |
| src/lib/rxdb.js | Modify | +4 collection schemas + replication handlers |

## Interfaces

### fn_determine_rcm_strategy(q1,q2,q3,q4,q5) RETURNS TEXT

| Q1 | Q2 | Q3 | Q4 | Q5 | Strategy |
| T  | —  | —  | —  | —  | BCM |
| F  | T  | —  | T  | —  | PM |
| F  | T  | —  | F  | T  | BCM |
| F  | T  | —  | F  | F  | REDESIGN |
| F  | F  | T  | T  | —  | PM |
| F  | F  | T  | F  | T  | BCM |
| F  | F  | T  | F  | F  | RTF |
| F  | F  | F  | —  | —  | RTF |

### rpn generated column: severity × occurrence × detection STORED

### Trigger trg_fmea_rcm_compute_strategy BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE

### Seed data: 10 types (BEA,SEA,SHA,IMP,MTR,VAL,GEA,BEL,COU,FIL), 38 failure modes

## Testing Strategy

| Layer | What | Approach |
| Schema | 4 tables, columns, constraints | pgTAP has_table(), has_column() |
| Constraints | CHECK, UNIQUE, FK | INSERT invalid values, verify rejection |
| Seed data | ≥10 types, 30-50 modes, ≥3 per type | COUNT queries |
| RCM function | All 8 rule branches | Call with known inputs, assert result |
| RLS | Each role × operation | SET ROLE + DML |
| COMMENT ON | All objects | obj_description() |

## Rollout

All new tables, no migration of existing data. DOWN: DROP 4 tables + function + trigger.

observations.title: FMEA/RCM seed data and RCM function implementation
observations.content:
**What**: Implemented FMEA/RCM module migration, tests, and RxDB integration
**Why**: Foundation for failure mode analysis and RCM strategy determination in the CMMS
**Where**: supabase/migrations/20260531000003_fmea_rcm_module_sdd1.sql, supabase/tests/database/20260531000003_fmea_rcm_module_sdd1_test.sql, src/lib/rxdb.js
**Learned**: 
- Used 10 component types: BEA, SEA, IMP, MTR, PUM, FAN, CPL, BLT, GEA, VAL (user-provided codes supersede design's SHA/BEL/COU/FIL)
- RCM function has 8 rule branches covering 32 boolean combos, returns BCM/PM/RTF/REDESIGN
- RPN is GENERATED ALWAYS AS (severity * occurrence * detection) STORED — prevents app-level inconsistency
- Failure mode codes are UNIQUE per component_type (not globally), allowing reuse (e.g., IMBALANCE for both IMP and FAN)

observations.title: sdd/fmea-rcm-module-sdd2/explore
observations.content:
## Exploration: SDD 2 — Corrective Failure Tracking

### Current State

#### Work Order Lifecycle (FSM)
The work order lifecycle follows ISO 14224 forward-only transitions:

```
WAPPR → APPROVED → INPRG → COMP → CLOSED
```

The mechanic interacts through `WorkOrderDrawer.jsx`:
- **APPROVED→INPRG**: "Iniciar" button — auto clock-in, checklist resolution
- **INPRG→COMP**: "Completar" button — validates notes (symptom_note, action_note are required), validates checklist gate (Block A must be PASS, hard blocks must be completed), auto clock-out. Then `onTransition(id, { lifecycle_phase: 'COMP', ...notes })` via `useWorkOrders.updateWorkOrder()` → RxDB upsert → Supabase push.
- **COMP→CLOSED**: "Cerrar" button — currently handled via `WorkOrderActions` (when `lifecyclePhase === 'COMP'`), but MechanicDashboard only filters `['WAPPR', 'APPROVED']`, so COMP→CLOSED is likely handled from a future PlannerDashboard or the existing WorkOrderActions component when it appears in a different view.

The actual DB transition is a RxDB document update → push handler → Supabase REST upsert. The Supabase side has a BEFORE UPDATE trigger (`validate_lifecycle_fsm`) that enforces forward-only transitions.

#### Existing Server-side Triggers on CLOSED
Two existing triggers fire at COMP→CLOSED — the patterns to follow:

1. **`trg_labor_sum_hours()`** (BEFORE UPDATE): When COMP→CLOSED, sums `labor_records.hours_worked` and writes to `work_orders.actual_hours`.
2. **`trg_condition_event_close_on_wo_closed()`** (AFTER UPDATE): When COMP→CLOSED and `condition_event_id` is set, auto-closes the associated `condition_event` (status→closed).

Both use the same guard pattern:
```sql
WHEN (NEW.lifecycle_phase = 'CLOSED' AND OLD.lifecycle_phase IS DISTINCT FROM 'CLOSED')
```

#### Existing ISO 14224 Failure Columns on work_orders
Dead columns (never populated in UI):
- `failure_class VARCHAR`, `problem_code VARCHAR`, `cause_code VARCHAR`, `remedy_code VARCHAR`
- `condition_event_id UUID` — FK to condition_events (populated by CBM trigger)
- `downtime_hours NUMERIC`
- `meter_id UUID` — FK to meters (populated by CBM trigger)

These exist in both Supabase schema and RxDB workOrderSchema, and are in `WORK_ORDER_PUSH_FIELDS`. They are **never populated** by any UI flow.

#### SDD 1 Tables (Deployed)
Migration `20260531000003_fmea_rcm_module_sdd1.sql` created:
- **`component_types`** — 10 ISO 14224 types
- **`asset_components`** — FK→assets, FK→component_types; UNIQUE(asset_id, name)
- **`failure_mode_catalog`** — 38 failure modes across 10 types
- **`fmea_rcm_analysis`** — FMEA/RPN + RCM decision tree → strategy

All 4 have RxDB collections + pull+push replication + RLS.

#### FocusModeModal Pattern
`FocusModeModal.jsx` is a full-screen Dialog opened from WorkOrderDrawer:
1. Detect incomplete Block A → show "Iniciar Cierre" button
2. Click → open FocusModeModal (rendered outside drawer)
3. Step through items one at a time with PASS/FAIL
4. On submit → RxDB write → re-check gate → allow "Completar"

This is the same pattern the failure recording modal should follow.

### Approaches Considered

1. **Server-side trigger only** — Auto-create failure_occurrence at COMP→CLOSED. Low effort, but misses mechanic input.
2. **FocusMode-style wizard + standalone editor** — Modal at COMP→CLOSED + planner editor. Medium-High effort, captures quality data. **RECOMMENDED**.
3. **Hybrid trigger + modal** — Trigger creates skeleton, modal supplements. High complexity, race conditions.

### Design Decisions

#### failure_occurrences Schema
```sql
CREATE TABLE failure_occurrences (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  work_order_id TEXT REFERENCES work_orders(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  asset_component_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES asset_components(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  failure_mode_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES failure_mode_catalog(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  cause_description TEXT,
  remedy_description TEXT,
  downtime_hours NUMERIC DEFAULT 0,
  created_by UUID,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ
);
-- work_order_id nullable for standalone editor entries
-- UNIQUE(work_order_id, asset_component_id, failure_mode_id) prevents duplicates
```

#### Relation to Existing Columns
**Complement, not replace.** `failure_occurrences` is structured analytics-grade data. The dead ISO 14224 columns remain on work_orders for now (deprecate in future phase).

#### Standalone Editor
`work_order_id` nullable for reliability engineer bulk/historical data entry. Standalone entries must have at minimum `asset_component_id` and `failure_mode_id`.

### Risks
- No PlannerDashboard exists yet for COMP→CLOSED or standalone editor
- Data quality: mechanics may not know which component failed
- Offline conflicts: UNIQUE constraint could reject concurrent duplicate pushes
- downtime_hours duplication between work_orders and failure_occurrences (different purposes)

### Ready for Proposal
Yes. All design questions answered. Recommend Approach 2 (FocusMode wizard).

observations.content:
# Spec: SDD 2 — Corrective Failure Tracking

## Domain: failure-occurrences

### Purpose

Track individual failure events at work order close-out, linked to SDD 1 catalogs (asset_components, failure_mode_catalog). Each row records what failed, how, why, and the downtime impact.

### R1: failure_occurrences Table

| Column | Type | Constraints |
|--------|------|-------------|
| id | UUID | PK, DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() |
| work_order_id | TEXT | FK → work_orders(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, NULLABLE |
| asset_component_id | UUID | NOT NULL, FK → asset_components(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT |
| failure_mode_id | UUID | NOT NULL, FK → failure_mode_catalog(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT |
| reported_at | TIMESTAMPTZ | NOT NULL, DEFAULT NOW() |
| downtime_hours | NUMERIC | NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, CHECK >= 0 |
| cause_description | TEXT | |
| remedy_description | TEXT | |
| created_by | UUID | DEFAULT auth.uid() |
| created_at | TIMESTAMPTZ | DEFAULT NOW() |

UNIQUE(work_order_id, asset_component_id, failure_mode_id) when work_order_id IS NOT NULL. COMMENT ON in Spanish.

### R2: RLS

TECHNICIAN: INSERT own (created_by=auth.uid()), SELECT own. PLANNER: ALL. ADMIN: ALL.

### R3: RxDB Collection

Pull+Push replication. Schema matching DDL. Conflict markers for UNIQUE.

### R4: Standalone Editor

PLANNER/ADMIN page at /_/failures for entries without WO linkage.

### Scenarios (10): Insert at close-out, duplicate rejection, NULL work_order_id allowed, negative downtime, cascade delete, technician own insert, technician cross-user rejection, planner full access, push replication, standalone entry creation.

## Domain: mechanic-work-order-execution (delta)

### MODIFIED — R2: Phase-Guided Actions

COMP → "Cerrar": if wo_type IN ('corrective','CBM'), opens FailureRecordingModal before transition. Other types transition immediately.

### ADDED — R13: Failure Recording Wizard

FailureRecordingModal: 4-step full-screen wizard (component → failure mode → cause+downtime → submit). "Omitir" writes unknown entry and proceeds. RxDB insert must succeed before CLOSED transition.

### Scenarios (6): Corrective WO modal flow, CBM prefilled, non-corrective skips, wizard step progression, unknown component, skip via Omitir, network error prevents transition.

**Why**: Per spec, corrective and CBM work orders require failure recording at close-out. Non-corrective WOs (preventive, predictive, etc.) close normally.
**Where**: `src/components/mechanic/WorkOrderDrawer.jsx` — handleConfirm() checks woType before executing CLOSED transition; handleFailureRecordingComplete() executes pending transition after modal submit/skip
**Learned**: The intercept uses a pending target pattern: confirm dialog sets pendingTarget, handleConfirm checks if woType requires failure recording. If yes, opens modal and defers transition. Modal completion triggers executeTransition(pendingTarget). This is a soft gate — the modal can be skipped via Omitir. The DB trigger only warns (WARNING), never blocks. CBM pre-fill pre-selects first asset component (simplified — full condition_event resolution needs additional schema).

Tu propuesta tiene fallas arquitectónicas graves para un sistema en producción. Rehace la propuesta corrigiendo lo siguiente:

Motor de Almacenamiento: RxDB ya no usa PouchDB. Actualiza las dependencias para usar el motor de almacenamiento Dexie (RxStorageDexie), que es el estándar actual para rendimiento.

Fiabilidad de Timestamps: No puedes usar Date.now() en el cliente para el pushHandler. Los relojes de los clientes no son confiables. El campo _last_modified debe ser gestionado por un Trigger en Supabase/PostgreSQL (ej. EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM NOW())). El cliente solo debe enviar la data, sin el timestamp.

Lógica del Checkpoint: En el pullHandler, el checkpoint de retorno NO debe ser Date.now(). Debe ser el _last_modified del documento más reciente que devolvió la consulta a Supabase.

Borrados (Deletes): Si un registro se borra en Supabase (_deleted: true), el pullHandler debe traerlo para que el cliente sepa que debe borrarlo localmente. Asegúrate de que la query de Supabase incluya los registros borrados en la sincronización.

Abstract
Recent advances in reasoning Large Language Models (LLMs) have primarily
relied on upfront thinking, where reasoning occurs before final answer. However,
this approach suffers from critical limitations in code generation, where upfront
thinking is often insufficient as problems’ full complexity only reveals itself during
code implementation. Moreover, it cannot adaptively allocate reasoning effort
throughout the code generation process where difficulty varies significantly. In this
paper, we propose THINK-ANYWHERE, a novel reasoning mechanism that enables
LLMs to invoke thinking on-demand at any token position during code generation.
We achieve THINK-ANYWHERE by first teaching LLMs to imitate the reasoning
patterns through cold-start training, then leveraging outcome-based RL rewards to
drive the model’s autonomous exploration of when and where to invoke reasoning.
Extensive experiments on four mainstream code generation benchmarks (i.e., LeetCode, LiveCodeBench, HumanEval, and MBPP) show that THINK-ANYWHERE
achieves state-of-the-art performance over both existing reasoning methods and
recent post-training approaches, while demonstrating consistent generalization
across diverse LLMs. Our analysis further reveals that THINK-ANYWHERE enables the model to adaptively invoke reasoning at high-entropy positions, providing
enhanced interpretability.

Los 3 Puntos Ciegos Industriales (Lo que dejaron fuera)
Punto Ciego 1: El "BOOLEAN" del resultado (PASS/FAIL) es una trampa
Ellos proponen que el resultado sea un simple TRUE/FALSE. En desarrollo eso se ve limpio, pero para la ingeniería de confiabilidad es un dato muerto.

El problema: Si el mecánico marca FAIL en "¿Utilizó el alineador láser?", el Competency Engine de GEMA solo sabrá que falló, pero no por qué.

La realidad: Si falló porque no sabe usarlo, la acción es Capacitación. Si falló porque el alineador láser está roto o guardado bajo llave, la acción es Inversión/Gestión. Un booleano no distingue entre un problema de habilidad y un problema de herramientas.

La Solución: Cambiar el campo result por un estado o agregar una columna de causa_falla (Catálogo corto: Falta de herramienta, Falta de conocimiento, Desviación intencional, No aplica).

Punto Ciego 2: ¿Quién es el "Sensor"? (Falta el evaluator_id)
El esquema de checklist_instances asume que el técnico se evalúa a sí mismo (technician_id).

El problema: Si el técnico se auto-evalúa para cerrar su orden de trabajo, por pura psicología laboral va a marcar PASS en todo para no meterse en problemas o terminar más rápido. El sistema se va a sesgar en una semana.

La realidad: Como acordamos, este sistema es un sensor de evidencia. Quien llena este bloque (especialmente el Bloque C de Precisión) suele ser el Supervisor durante un Spot Check (auditoría rápida) o el mecánico "A" que actúa como sinodal.

La Solución: La tabla checklist_instances debe incluir un campo evaluator_id (o verified_by). Si es una auto-evaluación se queda igual, pero si es una auditoría del supervisor, el sistema debe registrar quién avala esa evidencia.

Cuando el rodamiento de la Cavemil empieza a desgastarse, la firma de vibración cambia sutilmente (antes de que sea un problema visible). # Lo que está bien de la propuesta

Esto está bien pensado:

```sql
condition_readings
condition_features
```

La separación entre una **ventana de adquisición** y sus **features individuales** es correcta.

También está bien evitar columnas fijas porque tu sistema debe servir para:

* motor-bomba;
* transformador;
* compresor;
* ventilador;
* reductor;
* rutas manuales;
* sensores online;
* datos importados;
* instrumentos portátiles.

Si hardcodeas columnas por tipo de activo, el sistema muere rápido.

# El problema principal

La tabla:

```sql
condition_features (
  reading_id,
  feature_key,
  value,
  unit,
  quality
)
```

es flexible, pero demasiado libre.

El riesgo es que termines con basura semántica:

```text
vibration.rms_hv
vibration.rms.horizontal
vib.rms_h
rms_h
RMS_HV
```

Todas significando cosas parecidas.

O unidades inconsistentes:

```text
mm/s
mm/sec
mms
in/s
g
m/s2
```

Eso mata la escalabilidad.

Entonces necesitas una cosa más:

# Un catálogo de features

No basta con guardar `feature_key` como texto libre. Debe existir una tabla que gobierne qué significa cada feature.

Ejemplo:

```sql
condition_feature_definitions (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  feature_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  category TEXT NOT NULL,              -- vibr...

# Mi evaluación honesta

La propuesta original de:

```sql
condition_readings
condition_features
```

va bien porque EAV sirve justamente cuando tienes atributos dispersos o variables que cambian según el tipo de activo; es decir, cuando no sabes de antemano todas las columnas que vas a necesitar. Ese es tu caso: motor-bomba, transformador, compresor, medición manual, sensores online, etc. ([Wikipedia][1])

Pero EAV sin control semántico se vuelve desorden. Entonces el punto crítico no es “EAV sí o no”, sino:

> **EAV controlado por catálogo, no EAV libre.**

# En qué estoy de acuerdo con la otra IA

## 1. Multi-tenant puede esperar

Sí. Si hoy es una planta, un CMMS y un proyecto, no necesitas meter `organization_id` en todo desde el día uno.

Yo no lo bloquearía por eso.

Pero dejaría el diseño preparado así:

```sql
-- Fase futura
organization_id UUID DEFAULT '...'
```

No lo implementaría si te estorba, pero tampoco diseñaría algo que luego sea imposible migrar.

## 2. `value_text`, `value_bool`, `value_json` pueden esperar

Sí. Para Fase 1, si solo vas a guardar features numéricas, usa:

```sql
value_double DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL
```

Y listo.

No metas tipos de dato que todavía no vas a consumir.

## 3. `sensor_id`, `instrument_id`, `channel_id` pueden esperar parcialmente

Aquí matizo.

Para calcular HI, tal vez no necesitas el serial del sensor. Correcto.

Pero para trazabilidad metrológica futura, sí lo vas a necesitar. Entonces mi recomendación sería:

* no obligarlo en Fase 1;
* pero dejar columnas nullable o una tabla futura clara.

Ejemplo:

```sql
sensor_id UUID NULL
channel_id TEXT NULL
```

Yo no lo archivaría todavía sin una micro-revisión final, pero sí diría que la fase ya está prácticamente cerrada.

Los 3 críticos que detectaron eran realmente críticos, y los fixes que describes van en la dirección correcta:

condition_event_id en work_orders: necesario para trazabilidad.
anti-spam consultando condition_events en vez de hacer LIKE sobre texto: mucho mejor.
criticality derivada de severity: correcto para que la OT nazca priorizada.

Pero antes de archivar, revisaría estos puntos:

1. Endpoint reportado: posible error

Dices:

POST /rest/v1/ingest-condition
POST /rest/v1/ingest-events

Si son Supabase Edge Functions, normalmente no deberían exponerse como /rest/v1/..., sino como endpoint de función, tipo:

/functions/v1/ingest-condition
/functions/v1/ingest-events

/rest/v1 corresponde al API PostgREST de tablas/vistas/RPC, no a Edge Functions. No digo que esté mal si ustedes crearon algún proxy o ruta custom, pero tal como está escrito, yo lo marcaría como punto de verificación obligatorio.

2. Idempotencia de ingesta

Antes de archivar, asegúrate de que ingest-condition soporte reintentos sin duplicar ventanas.

En IIoT esto va a pasar:

el edge manda un FeatureSet;
se cae la red;
no sabe si llegó;
reintenta;
puedes duplicar condition_windows.

Necesitas algún idempotency_key o constraint natural, por ejemplo:

asset_id + window_start + window_end + source_id

o un external_reading_id generado por el edge.

Sin eso, el sistema se puede llenar de ventanas repetidas.

3. Anti-spam: 24 h puede ser demasiado rígido

La regla de anti-spam por:

asset_id + event_type + status dentro de 24h

es mucho mejor que el LIKE, pero tiene un riesgo:

puede bloquear una OT legítima si el mismo tipo de evento empeora dentro de 24 h;
o puede permitir duplicados si cambia levemente el event_type.

Yo lo dejaría para Fase 1, pero agregaría backlog:

anti_spam_policy configurable por asset_class / event_type / severity
